e.zh: 现在许多面包店都提供无麸质面包。

e.en: People with celiac disease must avoid {gluten} entirely.
e.zh: 乳糜泻患者必须完全避免摄入麸质。

e.en: The {gluteus} maximus is the largest muscle in the body.
e.zh: 臀大肌是人体中最大的肌肉。

e.en: Hip exercises target the {gluteus} medius effectively.
e.zh: 髋部训练能有效锻炼臀中肌。

e.en: This dessert is made with sweet {glutinous} rice.
e.zh: 这道甜点是用糯米做成的。

e.en: The sauce had a thick, {glutinous} texture.
e.zh: 这种酱料有着浓稠黏糊的质地。

glutted.t: v. 使充斥；塞满（glut 的过去式）

e.en: The market is {glutted} with cheap secondhand laptops.
e.zh: 市场上充斥着便宜的二手笔记本电脑。

e.en: Streaming services have {glutted} viewers with new shows.
e.zh: 流媒体平台让观众被新剧塞得满满当当。

e.en: He's a real {glutton} when it comes to chocolate cake.
e.zh: 一遇到巧克力蛋糕,他就成了十足的大胃王。

e.en: She's a {glutton} for punishment, working seven days a week.
e.zh: 她真是自讨苦吃,一周工作七天。

e.en: He felt guilty after his {gluttonous} holiday meal.
e.zh: 吃完那顿大快朵颐的节日大餐后他感到内疚。

e.en: The puppy gave a {gluttonous} look at the food bowl.
e.zh: 小狗用贪吃的眼神望着食盆。

e.en: Holiday feasts can easily turn into pure {gluttony}.
e.zh: 节日盛宴很容易变成纯粹的暴饮暴食。

e.en: The novel warns against the sin of {gluttony}.
e.zh: 这部小说警告人们不要犯暴食之罪。

e.en: White bread has a high {glycemic} index.
e.zh: 白面包的升糖指数很高。

e.en: Doctors recommend low-{glycemic} foods for diabetic patients.
e.zh: 医生建议糖尿病患者多吃低升糖指数的食物。

e.en: The lotion contains {glycerin} to keep skin soft.
e.zh: 这款乳液含有甘油，能让皮肤保持柔软。

e.en: Add a few drops of {glycerin} to the soap mixture.
e.zh: 在肥皂混合物中加入几滴甘油。

e.en: Bakers brush cakes with {glycerine} to lock in moisture.
e.zh: 烘焙师在蛋糕上刷甘油以锁住水分。

e.en: The cough syrup uses {glycerine} as a sweetener.
e.zh: 这种止咳糖浆用甘油作为甜味剂。

e.en: {Glycerol} is a byproduct of biodiesel production.
e.zh: 甘油是生物柴油生产的副产品。

e.en: Cells use {glycerol} as a backbone for fat molecules.
e.zh: 细胞用甘油作为脂肪分子的骨架。

e.en: The cream lists {glyceryl} stearate as an emulsifier.
e.zh: 这款面霜将甘油硬脂酸酯列为乳化剂。

e.en: {Glyceryl} trinitrate is prescribed for chest pain.
e.zh: 硝酸甘油可用于治疗胸痛。

e.en: {Glycine} is the smallest of the twenty amino acids.
e.zh: 甘氨酸是二十种氨基酸中最小的一种。

e.en: Some people take {glycine} supplements to sleep better.
e.zh: 有些人服用甘氨酸补充剂来改善睡眠。

e.en: The liver stores energy as {glycogen} between meals.
e.zh: 肝脏在两餐之间将能量以糖原形式储存。

e.en: Long runs deplete the muscle's {glycogen} reserves.
e.zh: 长跑会耗尽肌肉的糖原储备。

e.en: Antifreeze is mostly ethylene {glycol} mixed with water.
e.zh: 防冻液主要是乙二醇与水的混合物。

e.en: Propylene {glycol} is common in food and cosmetics.
e.zh: 丙二醇在食品和化妆品中很常见。

e.en: The virus uses a surface {glycoprotein} to enter cells.
e.zh: 病毒利用表面糖蛋白进入细胞。

e.en: Mucus is rich in {glycoprotein} molecules that trap dust.
e.zh: 黏液富含可捕获灰尘的糖蛋白分子。

e.en: Foxglove contains a cardiac {glycoside} used in heart drugs.
e.zh: 毛地黄含有一种用于心脏药物的强心苷。

e.en: Stevia leaves get their sweetness from a {glycoside}.
e.zh: 甜叶菊叶子的甜味来自一种糖苷。

e.en: Each ancient {glyph} on the wall told part of a story.
e.zh: 墙上每个古老的字符都讲述了故事的一部分。

e.en: The font designer redrew every {glyph} by hand.
e.zh: 字体设计师手工重绘了每一个字形。

e.en: Farmers spray {glyphosate} to kill weeds before planting.
e.zh: 农民在播种前喷洒草甘膦以除草。

e.en: Several countries are restricting {glyphosate} use over health concerns.
e.zh: 几个国家因健康问题限制使用草甘膦。

e.en: The union {GMB} is balloting members on a strike.
e.zh: GMB工会正在就罢工进行会员投票。

e.en: She joined {GMB} when she started working in the warehouse.
e.zh: 她到仓库工作后就加入了GMB工会。

gmbh.t: n. 德国有限责任公司

e.en: The startup registered as a {GmbH} in Berlin last year.
e.zh: 这家初创公司去年在柏林注册为有限责任公司。

e.en: Siemens {GmbH} signed a contract with the local supplier.
e.zh: 西门子有限公司与当地供应商签订了合同。

gmc.t: n. GMC（通用汽车旗下品牌）

e.en: He drives a black {GMC} pickup to work every morning.
e.zh: 他每天早上开一辆黑色GMC皮卡上班。

e.en: The new {GMC} Sierra has a redesigned interior.
e.zh: 新款GMC Sierra重新设计了内饰。

e.en: The recipe calls for 200 {gms} of flour.
e.zh: 这份食谱需要200克面粉。

e.en: Each cookie weighs about 30 {gms} when baked.
e.zh: 每块饼干烤好后约重30克。

gmt.t: n. 格林尼治标准时间

e.en: The meeting starts at 14:00 {GMT} sharp.
e.zh: 会议将于格林尼治标准时间14:00准时开始。

e.en: London uses {GMT} during the winter months.
e.zh: 伦敦在冬季使用格林尼治标准时间。

gnarled.t: adj. 粗糙多节的；扭曲的

e.en: The old farmer had {gnarled} hands from decades of work.
e.zh: 那位老农因数十年的劳作双手粗糙变形。

e.en: A {gnarled} oak tree stood at the edge of the field.
e.zh: 田边矗立着一棵盘根错节的老橡树。

e.en: That wave was absolutely {gnarly}, dude!
e.zh: 那个浪真是超猛的，老兄！

e.en: He tripped over a {gnarly} root on the trail.
e.zh: 他在小径上被一条扭曲的树根绊倒了。

e.en: Critics will {gnash} their teeth over the new policy.
e.zh: 批评者会对新政策咬牙切齿。

e.en: The dog began to {gnash} its teeth at the stranger.
e.zh: 那条狗开始对陌生人龇牙咆哮。

gnashing.t: v. 咬牙切齿（gnash 的现在分词）

e.en: There was much weeping and {gnashing} of teeth after the loss.
e.zh: 输球后大家哀嚎不已，咬牙切齿。

e.en: Fans were {gnashing} their teeth at the referee's call.
e.zh: 球迷们对裁判的判罚怒不可遏。

e.en: A {gnat} kept buzzing around my coffee cup.
e.zh: 一只小蚊子一直绕着我的咖啡杯飞。

e.en: Tiny {gnat} swarms hovered above the damp grass.
e.zh: 成群的小蚊子在潮湿的草地上方盘旋。

e.en: A blue-gray {gnatcatcher} flitted through the oak branches.
e.zh: 一只蓝灰蚋莺在橡树枝间飞来飞去。

e.en: Birders spotted a rare {gnatcatcher} near the wetland trail.
e.zh: 观鸟者在湿地步道附近发现了一只罕见的蚋莺。

e.en: Puppies love to {gnaw} on rubber toys.
e.zh: 小狗喜欢啃橡胶玩具。

e.en: Doubts began to {gnaw} at her confidence before the exam.
e.zh: 考试前疑虑开始侵蚀她的自信。

gnawed.t: v. 啃咬（gnaw 的过去式）

e.en: The mouse had {gnawed} a hole through the cereal box.
e.zh: 老鼠在麦片盒上啃出了一个洞。

e.en: Guilt {gnawed} at him long after the argument ended.
e.zh: 争吵结束后很久，内疚仍在折磨着他。

gnawing.t:
adj. 折磨人的
v. 啃咬（gnaw 的现在分词）

e.en: She had a {gnawing} feeling that something was wrong.
e.zh: 她隐隐觉得有什么不对劲。

e.en: The beaver was busy {gnawing} on a young tree.
e.zh: 那只海狸正忙着啃一棵小树。

gnaws.t: v. 啃咬（gnaw 的第三人称单数）

e.en: The puppy {gnaws} on its bone for hours.
e.zh: 小狗啃骨头能啃上好几个小时。

e.en: Regret still {gnaws} at him whenever he hears that song.
e.zh: 每当听到那首歌，悔恨仍折磨着他。

e.en: The cliff is made of ancient banded {gneiss}.
e.zh: 这座悬崖由古老的带状片麻岩构成。

e.en: Geologists collected samples of {gneiss} from the mountain.
e.zh: 地质学家从山上采集了片麻岩样本。

gnome.t: n. 地精；土地神（奇幻生物）

e.en: A ceramic {gnome} stood guard in the front garden.
e.zh: 一个陶瓷小矮人守在前花园里。

e.en: In the game, a {gnome} sells potions near the village.
e.zh: 游戏里有个侏儒在村庄附近卖药水。

e.en: The CEO gave a {gnomic} answer that puzzled reporters.
e.zh: 首席执行官的回答晦涩费解，让记者们摸不着头脑。

e.en: His tweets are famously {gnomic} and hard to interpret.
e.zh: 他的推文以晦涩著称，难以解读。

e.en: The sundial's {gnomon} cast a sharp shadow at noon.
e.zh: 日晷的指针在正午投下清晰的影子。

e.en: He carefully aligned the {gnomon} with true north.
e.zh: 他小心地把日晷指针对准正北。

e.en: The text describes a personal {gnosis} of the divine.
e.zh: 该文本描述了对神性的个人灵知。

e.en: Early sects pursued {gnosis} through meditation and study.
e.zh: 早期教派通过冥想和研习追求灵知。

gnostic.t: adj. 诺斯替教的；神秘知识的

e.en: The library held several rare {Gnostic} manuscripts.
e.zh: 图书馆收藏了几份珍稀的诺斯替手稿。

e.en: His novel borrows themes from {Gnostic} mythology.
e.zh: 他的小说借用了诺斯替神话的主题。

gnp.t: n. 国民生产总值（Gross National Product）

e.en: Economists track {GNP} to measure national income.
e.zh: 经济学家通过国民生产总值来衡量国民收入。

e.en: The country's {GNP} grew three percent last year.
e.zh: 该国去年的国民生产总值增长了百分之三。

e.en: A herd of {gnu} thundered across the savanna.
e.zh: 一群角马轰隆隆地穿过大草原。

e.en: Many programmers contribute to {GNU} software projects.
e.zh: 许多程序员为GNU软件项目做贡献。

e.en: We spent a week on the beaches of {Goa}.
e.zh: 我们在果阿的海滩上度过了一周。

e.en: {Goa} is famous for its seafood and Portuguese architecture.
e.zh: 果阿以海鲜和葡萄牙风格建筑闻名。

e.en: The cafeteria served some weird {glop} they called stew.
e.zh: 食堂端出一坨他们叫炖菜的奇怪糊糊。

e.en: A {glop} of paint dripped onto the new carpet.
e.zh: 一团油漆滴到了新地毯上。

e.en: The oatmeal turned into a {gloppy} mess on the stove.
e.zh: 燕麦粥在炉子上变成了黏糊糊的一团。

e.en: She hates {gloppy} sauces on her pasta.
e.zh: 她讨厌意面上裹着黏糊糊的酱汁。

gloria.t:
n. 荣耀颂（宗教赞美诗）
n. 女子名

e.en: The choir's soaring {gloria} filled the cathedral.
e.zh: 唱诗班高昂的荣耀颂响彻整座教堂。

e.en: Bach composed a famous {gloria} for the Christmas mass.
e.zh: 巴赫为圣诞弥撒谱写了一首著名的荣耀颂。

glories.t:
n. 荣耀（glory 的复数）
v. 自豪（第三人称单数）

e.en: The museum showcases the past {glories} of the empire.
e.zh: 博物馆展示着帝国昔日的辉煌。

e.en: He often retells the {glories} of his college football days.
e.zh: 他常常重述大学橄榄球时代的辉煌往事。

e.en: The film was criticized for its {glorification} of violence.
e.zh: 这部电影因美化暴力而受到批评。

e.en: Some worry social media leads to the {glorification} of wealth.
e.zh: 有人担心社交媒体在美化财富。

glorified.t:
adj. 被美化的
v. 赞美（过去式）

e.en: His new job title is just a {glorified} secretary role.
e.zh: 他的新头衔不过是个好听点的秘书职位。

e.en: Old soldiers are {glorified} in every national parade.
e.zh: 老兵在每次国家阅兵中都受到颂扬。

glorifies.t: v. 赞美；美化（第三人称单数）

e.en: The show {glorifies} a lifestyle most people can't afford.
e.zh: 这部剧美化了一种大多数人负担不起的生活方式。

e.en: The biography {glorifies} the founder while ignoring his flaws.
e.zh: 这本传记吹捧创始人却忽略了他的缺点。

e.en: Movies often {glorify} criminals and downplay the consequences.
e.zh: 电影常常美化罪犯,淡化后果。

e.en: We shouldn't {glorify} overworking as a badge of honor.
e.zh: 我们不该把过度工作美化成荣誉勋章。

glorifying.t: v. 赞美；美化（现在分词）

e.en: Critics accused the song of {glorifying} reckless driving.
e.zh: 批评者指责这首歌美化了鲁莽驾驶。

e.en: Stop {glorifying} hustle culture and get some sleep.
e.zh: 别再美化奋斗文化了,好好睡一觉。

gloriosa.t: n. 嘉兰（一种百合科植物）

e.en: A flame-red {gloriosa} climbed up the garden trellis.
e.zh: 一株火红的嘉兰沿着花园的格架向上攀爬。

e.en: The {gloriosa} lily is the national flower of Zimbabwe.
e.zh: 嘉兰百合是津巴布韦的国花。

e.en: We had a {glorious} sunny day at the beach.
e.zh: 我们在海滩度过了阳光灿烂的一天。

e.en: The team celebrated their {glorious} victory in the finals.
e.zh: 球队庆祝了他们在决赛中的辉煌胜利。

e.en: The garden was {gloriously} colorful in late spring.
e.zh: 晚春的花园色彩绚烂夺目。

e.en: She sang {gloriously} at the closing ceremony.
e.zh: 她在闭幕式上唱得无比动人。

glory.t:
n. 荣耀；荣誉
v. 自豪

e.en: The athlete trained for years to win Olympic {glory}.
e.zh: 这位运动员训练多年只为赢得奥运荣耀。

e.en: The cathedral was restored to its former {glory}.
e.zh: 这座大教堂被修复成了昔日的辉煌模样。

e.en: The address listed {Glos} as the abbreviation for Gloucestershire.
e.zh: 地址中用 Glos 作为格洛斯特郡的缩写。

e.en: Old maps often label the county simply as {Glos}.
e.zh: 旧地图常把这个郡简单地标为 Glos。

gloss.t:
n. 光泽；注释
v. 掩饰；注解

e.en: She applied a clear {gloss} to her lips.
e.zh: 她在嘴唇上涂了一层透明唇彩。

e.en: The report tries to {gloss} over serious problems.
e.zh: 这份报告试图掩饰严重的问题。

e.en: Check the {glossary} at the back of the textbook.
e.zh: 请查看教科书后面的术语表。

e.en: The app includes a handy {glossary} of medical terms.
e.zh: 这款应用收录了一份方便的医学术语表。

glossed.t: v. 加光泽；注解（过去式）

e.en: The manager {glossed} over the budget shortfall in the meeting.
e.zh: 经理在会上轻描淡写地带过了预算缺口。

e.en: She {glossed} her hair until it shone.
e.zh: 她把头发抹得油亮发光。

glossop.t: n. 格洛索普（英国地名/姓氏）

e.en: The train from Manchester to {Glossop} runs every half hour.
e.zh: 从曼彻斯特到格洛索普的火车每半小时一班。

e.en: {Glossop} is a small market town in Derbyshire.
e.zh: 格洛索普是德比郡的一个小集镇。

e.en: The magazine is printed on thick {glossy} paper.
e.zh: 这本杂志用厚厚的光面纸印刷。

e.en: Her dog has a beautiful {glossy} black coat.
e.zh: 她的狗有一身漂亮油亮的黑毛。

gloster.t: n. 格罗斯特（英国飞机公司/地名）

e.en: The {Gloster} Meteor was Britain's first jet fighter.
e.zh: 格罗斯特流星是英国第一款喷气式战斗机。

e.en: Collectors still admire the classic {Gloster} aircraft designs.
e.zh: 收藏家至今仍欣赏经典的格罗斯特飞机设计。

e.en: Many London speakers use a {glottal} stop instead of t.
e.zh: 许多伦敦人用喉塞音代替 t 音。

e.en: The linguist studied {glottal} sounds across dialects.
e.zh: 这位语言学家研究了各方言中的喉音。

e.en: The doctor examined her {glottic} area for signs of swelling.
e.zh: 医生检查了她声门区域是否有肿胀。

e.en: Surgeons use a special scope to view {glottic} structures.
e.zh: 外科医生用特殊内窥镜查看声门结构。

e.en: Air passes through the {glottis} when you speak or sing.
e.zh: 说话或唱歌时空气会经过声门。

e.en: Inflammation of the {glottis} can make breathing difficult.
e.zh: 声门发炎会让呼吸变得困难。

gloucester.t: n. 格洛斯特（英国城市）

e.en: We took a weekend trip to {Gloucester} to see the cathedral.
e.zh: 我们周末去格洛斯特参观了大教堂。

e.en: {Gloucester} is famous for its old docks and rugby team.
e.zh: 格洛斯特以其古老的码头和橄榄球队闻名。

gloucestershire.t: n. 格洛斯特郡（英国郡名）

e.en: My grandparents live in a quiet village in {Gloucestershire}.
e.zh: 我祖父母住在格洛斯特郡的一个安静村庄里。

e.en: {Gloucestershire} is known for its cheese-rolling festival.
e.zh: 格洛斯特郡以滚奶酪节而闻名。

e.en: He pulled a leather {glove} onto his right hand.
e.zh: 他把一只皮手套套在右手上。

e.en: Always wear a rubber {glove} when handling chemicals.
e.zh: 处理化学品时一定要戴橡胶手套。

e.en: The nurse gently checked the wound with a {gloved} hand.
e.zh: 护士戴着手套轻轻检查伤口。

e.en: A {gloved} hand reached out from the dark doorway.
e.zh: 一只戴着手套的手从黑暗的门口伸了出来。

e.en: His {gloveless} fingers turned red in the freezing wind.
e.zh: 他没戴手套的手指在寒风中冻得通红。

e.en: She rode her bike {gloveless} despite the cold morning.
e.zh: 尽管早晨很冷,她还是没戴手套骑车。

glover.t:
n. 手套制造商
n. 姓氏 格洛弗

e.en: The skilled {glover} crafted leather gloves for the queen.
e.zh: 这位熟练的手套匠为女王制作皮手套。

e.en: My neighbor's surname is {Glover}, an old English trade name.
e.zh: 我邻居姓 Glover,是个古老的英文行业姓氏。

e.en: Don't forget your {gloves} — it's freezing outside.
e.zh: 别忘了戴手套——外面冷得要命。

e.en: The boxer laced up his {gloves} before the match.
e.zh: 拳击手在比赛前系好了他的手套。

glow.t:
v. 发光；发热
n. 光辉

e.en: The candles cast a warm {glow} across the room.
e.zh: 烛光在房间里投下温暖的光晕。

e.en: Her cheeks {glow} after a long winter walk.
e.zh: 她在漫长的冬日散步后双颊泛红。

glower.t:
v. 怒目而视
n. 怒视

e.en: The old man would {glower} at noisy children on the bus.
e.zh: 那位老人会瞪着公车上吵闹的孩子们。

e.en: She gave him a long, dark {glower} across the table.
e.zh: 她隔着桌子久久地阴沉地瞪着他。

glowering.t:
adj. 怒视的
v. 怒视（现在分词）

e.en: He sat in the corner, {glowering} at his phone.
e.zh: 他坐在角落里,阴沉地盯着自己的手机。

e.en: The coach stood {glowering} as the team lost again.
e.zh: 球队再次输球时,教练阴沉着脸站在那里。

glowing.t: adj. 发光的；热情洋溢的

e.en: The book received {glowing} reviews from critics.
e.zh: 这本书得到了评论家的高度赞扬。

e.en: Embers were still {glowing} in the fireplace at midnight.
e.zh: 午夜时壁炉里的余烬还在发光。

glowingly.t: adv. 热烈地；赞不绝口地

e.en: Her teacher spoke {glowingly} about her progress this term.
e.zh: 老师对她本学期的进步赞不绝口。

e.en: Reviewers wrote {glowingly} of the new restaurant downtown.
e.zh: 评论员对市中心的这家新餐厅大加赞赏。

glows.t:
v. 发光（第三人称单数）
n. 光辉（复数）

e.en: The screen {glows} softly in the dark bedroom.
e.zh: 屏幕在漆黑的卧室里柔和地发着光。

e.en: Her face {glows} whenever she talks about her son.
e.zh: 每当她谈起儿子,脸上就会容光焕发。

e.en: We saw a tiny {glowworm} blinking on the forest path.
e.zh: 我们看见一只小萤火虫在林间小路上闪烁。

e.en: The cave is famous for its ceiling of {glowworm} lights.
e.zh: 这个洞穴以洞顶的萤光虫光闻名。

gluck.t: n. 格鲁克（作曲家姓氏）

e.en: Mozart was deeply influenced by the operas of {Gluck}.
e.zh: 莫扎特深受格鲁克歌剧的影响。

e.en: The orchestra performed a famous aria by {Gluck} tonight.
e.zh: 乐团今晚演奏了格鲁克的一首著名咏叹调。

e.en: Doctors often prescribe a {glucocorticoid} cream for severe rashes.
e.zh: 医生常给严重皮疹开糖皮质激素药膏。

e.en: Long-term {glucocorticoid} use can weaken the bones.
e.zh: 长期使用糖皮质激素会使骨骼变弱。

e.en: Many older adults take {glucosamine} for joint pain.
e.zh: 许多老年人服用氨基葡萄糖来缓解关节疼痛。

e.en: The vet recommended {glucosamine} supplements for our aging dog.
e.zh: 兽医建议给我们家年迈的狗补充氨基葡萄糖。

e.en: Diabetics must monitor their blood {glucose} levels daily.
e.zh: 糖尿病患者必须每天监测血糖水平。

e.en: The brain uses {glucose} as its main source of energy.
e.zh: 大脑以葡萄糖作为主要能量来源。

glue.t:
n. 胶水
v. 粘贴

e.en: Use a little {glue} to fix the broken handle.
e.zh: 用一点胶水把断了的把手粘好。

e.en: Trust is the {glue} that holds a team together.
e.zh: 信任是把团队凝聚在一起的黏合剂。

glued.t:
adj. 粘住的；紧盯的
v. 粘（过去式）

e.en: The kids stayed {glued} to the TV all afternoon.
e.zh: 孩子们整个下午都目不转睛地盯着电视。

e.en: She {glued} the photo into her scrapbook carefully.
e.zh: 她小心地把照片粘进剪贴簿里。

glug.t:
n. 咕嘟声
v. 咕嘟咕嘟地喝

e.en: He took a long {glug} of cold water after running.
e.zh: 他跑完步后大口大口地喝了一口凉水。

e.en: Add a {glug} of olive oil to the pan.
e.zh: 往锅里倒一些橄榄油。

glum.t: adj. 忧郁的；闷闷不乐的

e.en: He looked {glum} after losing the chess match.
e.zh: 输了那盘棋后他显得闷闷不乐。

e.en: The whole team felt {glum} about the rainy forecast.
e.zh: 整个团队对下雨的天气预报都感到沮丧。

e.en: She stared {glumly} out the window at the rain.
e.zh: 她郁郁地望着窗外的雨。

e.en: He nodded {glumly} and walked back to his desk.
e.zh: 他闷闷地点点头,走回了自己的办公桌。

e.en: A {gluon} binds quarks together inside protons and neutrons.
e.zh: 胶子将夸克束缚在质子和中子内部。

e.en: Physicists study how a {gluon} mediates the strong force.
e.zh: 物理学家研究胶子如何传递强相互作用力。

glut.t:
n. 供过于求
v. 使充满

e.en: There is a {glut} of new phones on the market.
e.zh: 市场上的新手机供过于求。

e.en: A {glut} of housing has pushed prices down.
e.zh: 房屋供应过剩拉低了价格。

e.en: Monosodium {glutamate} is widely used to enhance savory flavor.
e.zh: 味精被广泛用来增强咸鲜味。

e.en: {Glutamate} acts as a major neurotransmitter in the brain.
e.zh: 谷氨酸是大脑中一种主要的神经递质。

e.en: Athletes sometimes take {glutamine} to aid muscle recovery.
e.zh: 运动员有时服用谷氨酰胺来帮助肌肉恢复。

e.en: {Glutamine} is the most abundant amino acid in the blood.
e.zh: 谷氨酰胺是血液中含量最丰富的氨基酸。

goad.t:
v. 刺激；激怒
n. 刺棒

e.en: Don't let his comments {goad} you into a fight.
e.zh: 别让他的话挑唆你去打架。

e.en: Rivalry can {goad} athletes into peak performance.
e.zh: 竞争能激发运动员发挥出最佳水平。

goading.t: v. 激怒；驱使（goad 的现在分词）

e.en: He kept {goading} his brother until a fight broke out.
e.zh: 他一直挑衅哥哥，最后打了起来。

e.en: The crowd's {goading} only made the speaker more determined.
e.zh: 观众的起哄反而让演讲者更加坚定。

goal.t:
n. 目标
n. (足球) 进球；球门

e.en: Her main {goal} this year is to learn Mandarin.
e.zh: 她今年的主要目标是学好普通话。

e.en: Messi scored a stunning {goal} in the final minute.
e.zh: 梅西在最后一分钟打入了一个精彩的进球。

e.en: The {goalie} dove to her left and made the save.
e.zh: 门将向左扑出，扑出了这次射门。

e.en: Every kid wanted to be the {goalie} at recess.
e.zh: 课间休息时每个孩子都想当守门员。

e.en: The {goalkeeper} pulled off three saves in a row.
e.zh: 守门员连续三次扑救成功。

e.en: A young {goalkeeper} made his debut last weekend.
e.zh: 一位年轻门将上周末完成了首秀。

e.en: Modern {goalkeepers} need strong passing skills with their feet.
e.zh: 现代门将需要具备出色的脚下传球能力。

e.en: Two veteran {goalkeepers} are competing for the starting spot.
e.zh: 两位老将门将正在争夺首发位置。

e.en: Her {goalkeeping} kept the team in the tournament.
e.zh: 她的门将表现让球队留在了比赛中。

e.en: He took private lessons to improve his {goalkeeping}.
e.zh: 他上私教课来提升自己的守门技术。

goalless.t: adj. 无进球的；零比零的

e.en: The match ended in a dull {goalless} draw.
e.zh: 比赛以乏味的零比零平局收场。

e.en: Both teams played a tense {goalless} first half.
e.zh: 双方在紧张的上半场打成零比零。

e.en: There was a wild scramble in the {goalmouth} after the corner.
e.zh: 角球开出后，球门前一阵混战。

e.en: He cleared the ball from the {goalmouth} just in time.
e.zh: 他在最后关头把球从门前解围。

e.en: The shot crashed off the right {goalpost}.
e.zh: 那一脚射门击中了右侧门柱。

e.en: Kids used a backpack as a makeshift {goalpost}.
e.zh: 孩子们用书包当作临时球门柱。

e.en: Setting clear {goals} helps you stay motivated.
e.zh: 设定明确的目标有助于保持动力。

e.en: Haaland has scored thirty {goals} this season.
e.zh: 哈兰德本赛季已经攻入三十球。

e.en: He is the team's leading {goalscorer} this season.
e.zh: 他是球队本赛季的头号射手。

e.en: The young {goalscorer} signed a five-year contract.
e.zh: 这位年轻射手签下了一份五年合同。

e.en: The {goaltender} stopped forty-two shots in the playoff game.
e.zh: 这位守门员在季后赛中扑出了四十二次射门。

e.en: A backup {goaltender} stepped in after the injury.
e.zh: 主力受伤后，替补守门员顶了上去。

goaltending.t: n. 守门；干扰投篮（篮球违例）

e.en: Strong {goaltending} carried the team into the finals.
e.zh: 出色的守门表现把球队带进了决赛。

e.en: The referee called {goaltending} on the towering center.
e.zh: 裁判判罚那位高大的中锋干扰投篮。

e.en: A large {goanna} sunned itself on the warm rock.
e.zh: 一只大巨蜥趴在温热的岩石上晒太阳。

e.en: Hikers spotted a {goanna} crossing the bush track.
e.zh: 徒步者看到一只巨蜥穿过丛林小道。

e.en: The {goat} climbed onto the roof of the shed.
e.zh: 那只山羊爬上了棚屋的屋顶。

e.en: Many fans call Messi the {goat} of football.
e.zh: 许多球迷称梅西是足球史上最伟大的球员。

e.en: He grew a small {goatee} during the lockdown.
e.zh: 封锁期间他留起了一撮山羊胡。

e.en: The professor stroked his gray {goatee} thoughtfully.
e.zh: 教授若有所思地抚摸着灰色的山羊胡。

e.en: The {goatherd} led his flock up the mountain trail.
e.zh: 牧羊人带着羊群走上山路。

e.en: An old {goatherd} lived alone in the hills.
e.zh: 一位年迈的牧羊人独自住在山里。

e.en: The farmer keeps twenty {goats} on his land.
e.zh: 农夫在自家地里养了二十只山羊。

e.en: Wild {goats} roam freely across the rocky cliffs.
e.zh: 野山羊自由自在地在岩壁间漫步。

e.en: Travelers carried water in a {goatskin} bag.
e.zh: 旅人用山羊皮袋装水。

e.en: She bought a soft {goatskin} jacket in Morocco.
e.zh: 她在摩洛哥买了一件柔软的山羊皮夹克。

gob.t:
n. 一团（黏稠物）
n. 嘴（俚）

e.en: A {gob} of toothpaste fell into the sink.
e.zh: 一坨牙膏掉进了水槽里。

e.en: Shut your {gob} and listen for once.
e.zh: 闭上你的嘴,好好听一次。

e.en: She tossed a {gobbet} of meat to the dog.
e.zh: 她扔了一块肉给狗。

e.en: The article quoted a {gobbet} from his diary.
e.zh: 文章引用了他日记中的一小段。

gobble.t:
v. 狼吞虎咽地吃
v. (火鸡) 咯咯叫

e.en: Don't {gobble} your food so quickly at dinner.
e.zh: 吃晚饭时别狼吞虎咽。

e.en: Streaming services {gobble} up most of my data.
e.zh: 流媒体服务占用了我大部分流量。

gobbledegook.t: n. 晦涩难懂的官腔话

e.en: The contract was full of legal {gobbledegook}.
e.zh: 这份合同满是难懂的法律术语。

e.en: His explanation sounded like complete {gobbledegook} to me.
e.zh: 他的解释在我听来完全是莫名其妙的废话。

e.en: Tech manuals are often written in pure {gobbledygook}.
e.zh: 技术手册经常写得像天书一样。

e.en: Cut the {gobbledygook} and tell me the price.
e.zh: 少说废话,直接告诉我价格。

gobbler.t: n. 公火鸡；狼吞虎咽者

e.en: The wild {gobbler} strutted across the field at dawn.
e.zh: 那只野生雄火鸡黎明时分在田野里昂首阔步。

e.en: My nephew is a real food {gobbler} at parties.
e.zh: 我侄子在派对上真是个狼吞虎咽的家伙。

gobbling.t: v. 狼吞虎咽（gobble 的现在分词）

e.en: Stop {gobbling} the cookies before dinner is ready.
e.zh: 晚饭还没好,别再大口吃饼干了。

e.en: The app keeps {gobbling} battery in the background.
e.zh: 这个应用在后台不停地耗电。

e.en: Camels cross the {gobi} desert in long caravans.
e.zh: 骆驼组成长长的商队穿越戈壁沙漠。

e.en: We ordered aloo {gobi} at the Indian restaurant.
e.zh: 我们在印度餐厅点了土豆花椰菜。

e.en: She raised her crystal {goblet} for the toast.
e.zh: 她举起水晶高脚杯祝酒。

e.en: The knight drank wine from a silver {goblet}.
e.zh: 骑士用银制高脚杯喝酒。

e.en: A sneaky {goblin} guarded the treasure in the cave.
e.zh: 一个狡猾的妖怪守护着洞中的宝藏。

e.en: Kids dressed as a {goblin} for Halloween night.
e.zh: 孩子们万圣节晚上打扮成小妖怪。

e.en: The plot twist completely {gobsmack} the audience.
e.zh: 剧情反转让观众目瞪口呆。

e.en: That price will totally {gobsmack} you.
e.zh: 这个价格肯定会让你大吃一惊。

e.en: A small {goby} darted between the coral branches.
e.zh: 一条小虾虎鱼在珊瑚枝间穿梭。

e.en: Divers spotted a colorful {goby} near the reef.
e.zh: 潜水员在礁石附近发现了一条色彩斑斓的虾虎鱼。

e.en: Many cultures believe in a single creator {god}.
e.zh: 许多文化都信仰唯一的造物神。

e.en: Oh my {god}, you scared me half to death!
e.zh: 我的天啊,你吓死我了!

e.en: She bought her {godchild} a book for Christmas.
e.zh: 她给教子买了一本书作为圣诞礼物。

e.en: My {godchild} just started kindergarten this fall.
e.zh: 我的教子今秋刚上幼儿园。

e.en: Where did I put my {goddam} keys again?
e.zh: 我那该死的钥匙又放哪儿了?

e.en: Turn off that {goddam} alarm before I scream.
e.zh: 快关掉那该死的闹钟,不然我要喊了。

e.en: {Goddammit}, I forgot to save the document again.
e.zh: 该死,我又忘了保存文档。

e.en: {Goddammit}, the printer jammed right before the meeting.
e.zh: 该死,打印机偏偏在开会前卡纸了。

e.en: This {goddamn} traffic is making me late again.
e.zh: 这该死的堵车又让我迟到了。

e.en: I can't find my {goddamn} phone anywhere.
e.zh: 我到处都找不到那该死的手机。

e.en: Fix the {goddamned} leak before the floor warps.
e.zh: 在地板变形之前把那该死的漏水修好。

e.en: That {goddamned} cat knocked over the vase again.
e.zh: 那只该死的猫又把花瓶打翻了。

e.en: My {goddaughter} graduated from college this spring.
e.zh: 我的教女今年春天大学毕业了。

e.en: He sent his {goddaughter} flowers on her birthday.
e.zh: 他在教女生日时送了她鲜花。

e.en: Athena was the Greek {goddess} of wisdom and war.
e.zh: 雅典娜是希腊智慧与战争的女神。

e.en: Fans treat the singer like a pop {goddess}.
e.zh: 粉丝们把那位歌手当成流行女神。

e.en: Ancient temples were dedicated to various {goddesses}.
e.zh: 古代神庙是为各位女神而建的。

e.en: The novel features powerful {goddesses} from many cultures.
e.zh: 这部小说讲述了许多文化中强大的女神。

godfather.t:
n. 教父
n. 黑帮教父

e.en: My {godfather} taught me how to ride a bike.
e.zh: 我的教父教我骑自行车。

e.en: He is widely called the {godfather} of hip-hop.
e.zh: 他被广泛称为嘻哈音乐的教父。

e.en: We drove for hours through {godforsaken} desert highways.
e.zh: 我们开了几小时车穿越荒凉的沙漠公路。

e.en: Why would anyone live in this {godforsaken} place?
e.zh: 谁会愿意住在这种鸟不拉屎的地方?

e.en: Theologians debated the nature of the {godhead} for centuries.
e.zh: 神学家们就神性的本质争论了几个世纪。

e.en: The text describes the {godhead} as eternal and unchanging.
e.zh: 经文将神格描述为永恒不变的。

e.en: In the myth, the hero ascends to {godhood}.
e.zh: 在神话中,英雄最终升格为神。

e.en: Emperors once claimed {godhood} to justify their rule.
e.zh: 皇帝曾自称神格以巩固统治。

godiva.t: n. 戈黛娃（夫人，传说人物）

e.en: She bought a box of {godiva} chocolates as a gift.
e.zh: 她买了一盒歌帝梵巧克力当礼物。

e.en: Lady {godiva} famously rode through the streets of Coventry.
e.zh: 戈黛娃夫人因骑马穿越考文垂街道而闻名。

godless.t: adj. 不信神的；无神论的

e.en: Critics called the new regime cruel and {godless}.
e.zh: 批评者称新政权残忍且毫无敬畏之心。

e.en: The novel imagines a {godless} future society.
e.zh: 这部小说设想了一个无神的未来社会。

godlessness.t: n. 不信神；无神论状态

e.en: The preacher warned against the {godlessness} of modern life.
e.zh: 传教士警告人们要警惕现代生活的不敬神。

e.en: He blamed the city's troubles on widespread {godlessness}.
e.zh: 他把城市的种种问题归咎于普遍的不敬神。

e.en: The athlete moved with {godlike} grace and power.
e.zh: 那位运动员以神一般的优雅和力量奔跑。

e.en: Tech billionaires are sometimes given {godlike} status online.
e.zh: 科技亿万富翁有时在网上被奉若神明。

e.en: Cleanliness is next to {godliness}, my grandmother always said.
e.zh: 我外婆常说,洁净仅次于敬神。

e.en: The monks pursued {godliness} through prayer and silence.
e.zh: 修士们通过祈祷与沉默追求虔敬。

e.en: She tried to live a {godly} and humble life.
e.zh: 她努力过一种虔敬而谦卑的生活。

e.en: His parents raised him with strict {godly} values.
e.zh: 他的父母用严格的虔诚价值观养育他。

e.en: Her {godmother} sends her a card every birthday.
e.zh: 她的教母每年生日都寄给她一张贺卡。

e.en: The fairy {godmother} granted Cinderella one magical wish.
e.zh: 仙女教母给了灰姑娘一个神奇的愿望。

e.en: The {godolphin} stable produced many champion racehorses.
e.zh: 高多芬马场培育出了许多冠军赛马。

e.en: He read a biography of Sidney {godolphin} last weekend.
e.zh: 他上周末读了一本关于西德尼·戈多尔芬的传记。

e.en: Choosing a {godparent} is an important family decision.
e.zh: 选择教父母是家庭中的重要决定。

e.en: Each {godparent} promised to support the child's upbringing.
e.zh: 每位教父母都承诺支持孩子的成长。

gods.t: n. 神；神明（god 的复数）

e.en: The ancient Greeks worshipped many different {gods}.
e.zh: 古希腊人崇拜许多不同的神。

e.en: Thank the {gods}, the rain finally stopped.
e.zh: 谢天谢地,雨终于停了。

godsend.t: n. 及时雨；意外的好事

e.en: This new dishwasher has been an absolute {godsend}.
e.zh: 这台新洗碗机简直是天赐之物。

e.en: Remote work was a {godsend} for working parents.
e.zh: 远程工作对在职父母来说是天赐之福。

e.en: He took his {godson} to the baseball game.
e.zh: 他带教子去看棒球比赛。

e.en: My {godson} just turned ten years old yesterday.
e.zh: 我的教子昨天刚满十岁。

goer.t: n. 常去某地的人；进行者

e.en: She's a regular church-{goer} in her neighborhood.
e.zh: 她是社区里常去教堂的人。

e.en: As a frequent movie-{goer}, he reviews every new release.
e.zh: 作为常去电影院的人,他每部新片都写评论。

goes.t: v. go 的第三人称单数

e.en: The bus {goes} downtown every fifteen minutes.
e.zh: 这趟公交车每十五分钟开往市中心。

e.en: He {goes} jogging in the park before work.
e.zh: 他上班前会去公园慢跑。

e.en: As an intern, he was basically the office {gofer}.
e.zh: 作为实习生,他基本上就是办公室的跑腿。

e.en: She's tired of being a {gofer} for the senior staff.
e.zh: 她厌倦了为高级员工跑腿打杂。

e.en: The Bible mentions {gog} and Magog as legendary enemies.
e.zh: 圣经将歌革和玛各描述为传说中的敌人。

e.en: He bought the game on {gog} during the sale.
e.zh: 他在打折时从GOG平台买了这款游戏。

goggle.t:
v. 瞪大眼睛看
n. 护目镜（常用复数 goggles）

e.en: Children {goggle} at the giant whale in the aquarium.
e.zh: 孩子们瞪大眼睛看着水族馆里的大鲸鱼。

e.en: Tourists {goggle} at the dazzling lights of Times Square.
e.zh: 游客们目瞪口呆地看着时代广场的炫目灯光。

e.en: Where are you {goin} this weekend with your friends?
e.zh: 这个周末你和朋友们要去哪里?

e.en: I'm {goin} to grab some coffee, want any?
e.zh: 我去买杯咖啡,你要吗?

going.t:
n. 进展；去
adj. 正在进行的；现行的

e.en: I'm {going} to the gym after work today.
e.zh: 我今天下班后要去健身房。

e.en: The road conditions made the driving very tough {going}.
e.zh: 路况让这趟车开得非常艰难。

goiter.t: n. 甲状腺肿大（大脖子病）

e.en: Iodine deficiency can cause a noticeable {goiter} in the neck.
e.zh: 碘缺乏会导致颈部出现明显的甲状腺肿。

e.en: The doctor examined the patient's {goiter} during the checkup.
e.zh: 医生在检查时仔细查看了病人的甲状腺肿。

e.en: The {Golan} Heights remain a disputed border region.
e.zh: 戈兰高地至今仍是有争议的边境地区。

e.en: He hiked through the {Golan} during his trip to Israel.
e.zh: 他在以色列旅行时徒步穿越了戈兰地区。

gold.t:
n. 黄金；金色
adj. 金色的

e.en: She won the {gold} medal in the 200-meter sprint.
e.zh: 她在两百米短跑中赢得了金牌。

e.en: The price of {gold} hit a record high last month.
e.zh: 上个月黄金价格创下了历史新高。

goldbrick.t:
v. 偷懒；磨洋工
n. 冒牌货

e.en: Don't be a {goldbrick} when the team needs help.
e.zh: 团队需要帮忙时别偷懒摸鱼。

e.en: The manager fired the {goldbrick} who skipped meetings.
e.zh: 经理解雇了那个总翘会议的混日子员工。

golden.t: adj. 金色的；黄金的；宝贵的

e.en: Now is a {golden} opportunity to invest in tech.
e.zh: 现在是投资科技行业的黄金机会。

e.en: The fields turned {golden} under the autumn sun.
e.zh: 田野在秋日阳光下变成了金黄色。

e.en: Bees love the bright {goldenrod} flowers in late summer.
e.zh: 蜜蜂喜爱夏末盛开的金黄色一枝黄花。

e.en: She painted the kitchen walls a soft {goldenrod} yellow.
e.zh: 她把厨房墙壁刷成了柔和的一枝黄花色。

golders.t: n. 戈德斯（地名，如 Golders Green）

e.en: We had bagels at a deli in {Golders} Green.
e.zh: 我们在金德斯绿地的熟食店吃了贝果。

e.en: {Golders} Green is a famous Jewish neighborhood in London.
e.zh: 金德斯绿地是伦敦著名的犹太人社区。

e.en: Miners flocked to the Australian {goldfield} in the 1850s.
e.zh: 十九世纪五十年代矿工们涌向澳大利亚金矿区。

e.en: The old {goldfield} is now a popular tourist site.
e.zh: 那片旧金矿区如今成了热门旅游景点。

e.en: A bright yellow {goldfinch} landed on the bird feeder.
e.zh: 一只亮黄色的金翅雀停在喂鸟器上。

e.en: The {goldfinch} sang sweetly from the apple tree.
e.zh: 金翅雀在苹果树上甜美地歌唱。

goldfinger.t: n. 金手指（007 电影反派）

e.en: {Goldfinger} remains one of the most iconic Bond films.
e.zh: 《金手指》至今仍是最经典的邦德电影之一。

e.en: The villain in {Goldfinger} wanted to rob Fort Knox.
e.zh: 《金手指》里的反派想要洗劫诺克斯堡。

e.en: My daughter won a {goldfish} at the school fair.
e.zh: 我女儿在学校集市上赢了一条金鱼。

e.en: Don't overfeed the {goldfish} or the water gets dirty.
e.zh: 别给金鱼喂太多,否则水会变脏。

e.en: This vintage shop is a {goldmine} for collectors.
e.zh: 这家古董店对收藏家来说简直是宝藏。

e.en: The startup turned out to be a real {goldmine}.
e.zh: 那家初创公司最后成了一座真正的金矿。

e.en: The {goldsmith} carefully shaped the ring by hand.
e.zh: 金匠仔细地用手打造那枚戒指。

e.en: Her grandfather was a famous {goldsmith} in Florence.
e.zh: 她的祖父是佛罗伦萨一位著名的金匠。

golem.t: n. 魔像；傀儡（犹太传说泥人）

e.en: In Jewish folklore, a {golem} is made from clay.
e.zh: 在犹太民间传说中,魔像是用黏土做成的。

e.en: The novel features a {golem} that protects the village.
e.zh: 那部小说讲述了一个守护村庄的魔像。

golf.t:
n. 高尔夫球运动
v. 打高尔夫

e.en: My dad plays {golf} every Saturday morning.
e.zh: 我爸每个周六早上都去打高尔夫。

e.en: The {golf} course was packed during the tournament.
e.zh: 比赛期间高尔夫球场挤满了人。

e.en: She's the best amateur {golfer} in the club.
e.zh: 她是俱乐部里最出色的业余高尔夫球手。

e.en: The professional {golfer} signed autographs after the match.
e.zh: 那位职业高尔夫球手在比赛后签了名。

golfers.t: n. 打高尔夫球的人（复数）

e.en: Several {golfers} were waiting at the first tee.
e.zh: 好几位高尔夫球手在第一发球台等候。

e.en: Pro {golfers} train for hours to perfect their swing.
e.zh: 职业高尔夫球手要练上几个小时才能完善挥杆。

golfing.t:
n. 打高尔夫球
v. golf 的现在分词

e.en: Dad spent the weekend {golfing} with his old friends.
e.zh: 爸爸整个周末都和老朋友们打高尔夫去了。

e.en: Scotland is a famous destination for {golfing} enthusiasts.
e.zh: 苏格兰是高尔夫爱好者的著名度假胜地。

goliath.t: n. 歌利亚；巨人、庞然大物

e.en: The startup took on a tech {goliath} and won.
e.zh: 那家初创公司挑战科技巨头并取得了胜利。

e.en: David defeated {Goliath} with just a sling and stone.
e.zh: 大卫仅用投石器和一块石头打败了歌利亚。

golliwog.t: n. 黑脸布娃娃（旧式玩偶）

e.en: The old {golliwog} doll is now considered offensive.
e.zh: 那种老式的黑人布娃娃如今被视为带有冒犯性。

e.en: Many museums removed the {golliwog} from their displays.
e.zh: 许多博物馆已将那种黑人玩偶从展品中撤下。

e.en: {Golly}, I didn't expect the bill to be so high!
e.zh: 天哪,我没想到账单这么贵!

e.en: "By {golly}, you finally fixed the car!" he laughed.
e.zh: “老天,你终于把车修好了!”他笑道。

gomorrah.t: n. 蛾摩拉（圣经罪恶之城）

e.en: The Bible describes Sodom and {Gomorrah} as wicked cities.
e.zh: 圣经把所多玛和蛾摩拉描述为邪恶之城。

e.en: The film {Gomorrah} portrays the Naples crime underworld.
e.zh: 电影《格莫拉》描绘了那不勒斯的犯罪黑社会。

e.en: The {gonad} produces both hormones and reproductive cells.
e.zh: 性腺既产生激素也产生生殖细胞。

e.en: Biology class today covered how the {gonad} develops.
e.zh: 今天的生物课讲了性腺是如何发育的。

e.en: The doctor ordered tests to check {gonadal} function.
e.zh: 医生开了检查来评估性腺功能。

e.en: Hormone therapy can affect {gonadal} development in teenagers.
e.zh: 激素治疗可能影响青少年的性腺发育。

e.en: The clinic uses {gonadotropin} to stimulate egg production.
e.zh: 诊所使用促性腺激素来促进卵子生成。

e.en: Doctors monitor {gonadotropin} levels during fertility treatments.
e.zh: 医生在生育治疗期间监测促性腺激素水平。

gondola.t: n. 贡多拉（威尼斯小船）；缆车车厢

e.en: We rode a {gondola} through the canals of Venice.
e.zh: 我们乘坐贡多拉穿过威尼斯的运河。

e.en: The ski {gondola} carried us to the mountain summit.
e.zh: 滑雪缆车把我们送到了山顶。

e.en: The {gondolier} sang softly as we glided past palaces.
e.zh: 贡多拉船夫轻声哼唱,我们滑过座座宫殿。

e.en: A skilled {gondolier} can navigate Venice's narrowest canals.
e.zh: 熟练的船夫能在威尼斯最窄的运河中穿行。

gone.t:
adj. 离去的、消失的
v. go 的过去分词

e.en: By the time I arrived, everyone had already {gone}.
e.zh: 等我到的时候,大家都已经走了。

e.en: All the cookies were {gone} within five minutes.
e.zh: 所有饼干在五分钟内就被吃光了。

goner.t: n. 没救的人、完蛋的家伙

e.en: If the boss finds out, you're a {goner}.
e.zh: 老板要是发现了,你就完蛋了。

e.en: The plant looked like a {goner} after the frost.
e.zh: 那盆植物经过霜冻看起来已经没救了。

e.en: The dinner {gong} echoed through the old hotel.
e.zh: 晚餐锣声在那家老酒店里回荡。

e.en: He struck the {gong} to start the ceremony.
e.zh: 他敲响铜锣以开启仪式。

e.en: The therapist used a {goniometer} to measure my knee angle.
e.zh: 治疗师用量角仪测量了我的膝盖角度。

e.en: A {goniometer} helps assess joint range of motion.
e.zh: 量角仪有助于评估关节的活动范围。

e.en: The study used {goniometric} measurements to track recovery.
e.zh: 研究采用关节角度测量来追踪康复进展。

e.en: {Goniometric} analysis revealed improved flexibility after therapy.
e.zh: 角度测量分析显示治疗后柔韧性有所提升。

e.en: Doctors warn that {gonorrhea} is becoming antibiotic-resistant.
e.zh: 医生警告淋病正在产生抗生素耐药性。

e.en: Regular testing helps detect {gonorrhea} early.
e.zh: 定期检查有助于及早发现淋病。

e.en: The clinic provides free {gonorrhoea} screening for young adults.
e.zh: 诊所为年轻人提供免费的淋病筛查。

e.en: Untreated {gonorrhoea} can lead to serious complications.
e.zh: 未经治疗的淋病可能导致严重并发症。

e.en: The kids made sticky {goo} from glue and borax.
e.zh: 孩子们用胶水和硼砂做出了黏糊糊的胶泥。

e.en: There's some weird green {goo} stuck to the floor.
e.zh: 地板上粘着一些奇怪的绿色黏液。

e.en: He's such a {goober}, but everyone loves him.
e.zh: 他真是个傻乎乎的家伙,不过大家都喜欢他。

e.en: In the South, peanuts are sometimes called {goober} nuts.
e.zh: 在美国南方,花生有时被叫做goober。

good.t:
adj. 好的、优秀的
n. 好处、善

e.en: That was a really {good} movie—I'd watch it again.
e.zh: 那真是部好电影,我愿意再看一遍。

e.en: She's {good} at explaining complicated math problems.
e.zh: 她很擅长讲解复杂的数学题。

e.en: Her brother is tall and surprisingly {good-looking}.
e.zh: 她哥哥个子高,长得还挺帅。

e.en: That's a {good-looking} car you bought last week.
e.zh: 你上周买的那辆车真好看。

e.en: He waved {goodby} as the train pulled out of the station.
e.zh: 火车驶离车站时他挥手告别。

e.en: She whispered {goodby} and quietly closed the door.
e.zh: 她轻声道别,悄悄关上了门。

goodbye.t:
int. 再见
n. 告别

e.en: We said {goodbye} at the airport with tears in our eyes.
e.zh: 我们在机场含泪道别。

e.en: It's hard to say {goodbye} after so many years together.
e.zh: 在一起这么多年后,告别真的很难。

e.en: The {goodbyes} at graduation lasted nearly an hour.
e.zh: 毕业典礼上的告别持续了近一个小时。

e.en: She hates long {goodbyes} and always leaves quickly.
e.zh: 她讨厌冗长的告别,总是走得很快。

goodie.t: n. 好东西、好吃的；好人

e.en: Each child got a {goodie} bag at the birthday party.
e.zh: 生日派对上每个孩子都拿到一个小礼袋。

e.en: Grandma always has a {goodie} hidden in her purse.
e.zh: 奶奶包里总藏着一份小零食。

goodies.t: n. 好吃的、好东西（复数）

e.en: The bakery box was full of {goodies} for the kids.
e.zh: 那个面包店的盒子里装满了孩子们爱吃的零食。

e.en: Subscribers get exclusive {goodies} every month.
e.zh: 订阅者每月都能获得专属福利。

e.en: The fundraiser collected a {goodly} sum for the shelter.
e.zh: 这次募捐为庇护所筹得了相当可观的一笔钱。

e.en: He inherited a {goodly} portion of his uncle's estate.
e.zh: 他继承了叔父相当大一部分遗产。

e.en: The {goodman} of the house welcomed every guest warmly.
e.zh: 这家的男主人热情地欢迎每一位客人。

e.en: In old tales, the {goodman} farmer worked from dawn to dusk.
e.zh: 在古老的故事里,那位农夫从早干到晚。

goodness.t:
n. 善良、美德
int. 天哪

e.en: Oh my {goodness}, look at how big he's grown!
e.zh: 我的天啊,看他长得多高了!

e.en: There's still {goodness} in people, even in tough times.
e.zh: 即使在艰难时刻,人间仍有善意。

e.en: The poet praised the small {goodnesses} of everyday life.
e.zh: 诗人赞美日常生活中那些小小的美好。

e.en: We often overlook the simple {goodnesses} around us.
e.zh: 我们常常忽视身边那些朴素的善意。

e.en: She kissed her son {goodnight} and turned off the lamp.
e.zh: 她吻别儿子道晚安,然后关上了灯。

e.en: "{Goodnight}, sleep tight," Dad said from the doorway.
e.zh: “晚安,睡个好觉,”爸爸在门口说道。

e.en: The store sells imported {goods} from all over Asia.
e.zh: 这家店销售来自亚洲各地的进口商品。

e.en: Damaged {goods} can be returned within thirty days.
e.zh: 损坏的商品可在三十天内退换。

goodwife.t: n. 主妇（旧时对已婚妇女的称呼）

e.en: The {goodwife} baked bread for the entire village.
e.zh: 那位主妇为全村人烤了面包。

e.en: In colonial times, every {goodwife} managed the household economy.
e.zh: 在殖民地时期,每位主妇都掌管家庭经济。

goodwill.t:
n. 善意、好感
n. 商誉（会计）

e.en: The donation was a gesture of {goodwill} toward neighbors.
e.zh: 这次捐款是向邻居们表达善意的举动。

e.en: Acquiring the brand added significant {goodwill} to our balance sheet.
e.zh: 收购该品牌为我们的资产负债表增加了大量商誉。

e.en: The merger valued the {goodwills} of both brands at millions.
e.zh: 合并时双方品牌的商誉被估值数百万。

e.en: Companies often list {goodwills} as intangible assets on balance sheets.
e.zh: 公司常把商誉作为无形资产列入资产负债表。

goodwood.t: n. 古德伍德（英国地名）

e.en: We watched the classic car race at {Goodwood} last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末我们在古德伍德观看了经典车比赛。

e.en: The {Goodwood} Festival of Speed attracts fans from around the world.
e.zh: 古德伍德速度节吸引着世界各地的车迷。

goody.t:
n. 好吃的、好玩的东西
int. 太好啦

e.en: The kids cheered and shouted {goody} when dessert arrived.
e.zh: 甜点端上来时孩子们欢呼着喊“太好啦”。

e.en: Each guest received a small {goody} bag at the party.
e.zh: 每位客人在派对上都收到了一个小礼品袋。

e.en: The car came with a fresh set of {Goodyear} tires.
e.zh: 这辆车配了一套全新的固特异轮胎。

e.en: A {Goodyear} blimp floated above the stadium during the game.
e.zh: 比赛期间一艘固特异飞艇飘在体育场上空。

e.en: The chocolate brownies were warm and {gooey} in the middle.
e.zh: 巧克力布朗尼中间又温热又黏糊。

e.en: My fingers got {gooey} after peeling the ripe mango.
e.zh: 剥完熟芒果后我的手指变得黏糊糊的。

goof.t:
v. 出错、犯傻
n. 蠢事、笨蛋

e.en: Don't {goof} around during the meeting—we have a deadline.
e.zh: 开会时别瞎闹——我们有截止日期。

e.en: I made a silly {goof} on the spreadsheet formula.
e.zh: 我在表格公式里犯了个愚蠢的错误。

e.en: My little brother is such a {goofball} at family dinners.
e.zh: 我弟弟在家庭聚餐上简直是个活宝。

e.en: The comedian plays a lovable {goofball} in the new sitcom.
e.zh: 那位喜剧演员在新情景剧里饰演一个可爱的傻瓜。

e.en: His {goofiness} always lightens the mood in tense meetings.
e.zh: 他的搞怪总能在紧张的会议中缓和气氛。

e.en: The puppy's {goofiness} made everyone in the park laugh.
e.zh: 那只小狗的傻萌逗得公园里的人都笑了。

e.en: He pulled a {goofy} face for the selfie.
e.zh: 他自拍时做了个傻乎乎的鬼脸。

e.en: The app has a {goofy} mascot that dances when you score.
e.zh: 这款应用有个傻气的吉祥物,得分时会跳舞。

googol.t: n. 古戈尔（10 的 100 次方）

e.en: A {googol} is one followed by a hundred zeros.
e.zh: 古戈尔是1后面跟着一百个零。

e.en: Google's name was inspired by the huge number called a {googol}.
e.zh: 谷歌的名字灵感来自一个叫古戈尔的巨大数字。

gook.t: n. 黏糊糊的脏东西（俚，带歧视色彩）

e.en: There was sticky {gook} stuck under the kitchen sink.
e.zh: 厨房水槽下面粘着一坨黏糊糊的脏东西。

e.en: He scraped the black {gook} off the engine parts.
e.zh: 他把发动机零件上的黑色油垢刮掉了。

e.en: The mechanic wiped greasy {gooks} from the old machinery.
e.zh: 机修工把旧机器上的油污一团团擦掉。

e.en: Strange {gooks} of paint had hardened in the abandoned cans.
e.zh: 废弃罐子里几团油漆已经凝固成块。

e.en: The freight train stopped briefly at {Goole} on its route.
e.zh: 那列货运列车在途中曾在古尔短暂停靠。

e.en: {Goole} is a port town in East Yorkshire, England.
e.zh: 古尔是英格兰东约克郡的一座港口小镇。

e.en: The kids called the slime a {gooly} mess on the floor.
e.zh: 孩子们把地上那摊黏液叫做一坨黏糊糊的东西。

e.en: He gave a {gooly} grin after winning the silly contest.
e.zh: 赢了那场搞笑比赛后他咧嘴傻笑。

goon.t:
n. 打手、恶棍
n. 蠢货

e.en: A hired {goon} blocked the entrance to the warehouse.
e.zh: 一名受雇的打手堵在仓库门口。

e.en: Stop acting like a {goon} and take this seriously.
e.zh: 别像个二愣子一样,认真点对待这件事。

e.en: Some sticky {goop} leaked out of the broken pen.
e.zh: 破钢笔里渗出了一些黏糊糊的东西。

e.en: He squeezed green {goop} onto his hair before styling it.
e.zh: 他在头发上挤了点绿色发胶,然后开始造型。

e.en: The face mask felt cold and {goopy} on my skin.
e.zh: 那款面膜敷在皮肤上又凉又黏糊。

e.en: She stirred the {goopy} batter until it was smooth.
e.zh: 她把那团黏糊糊的面糊搅拌到顺滑。

goose.t:
n. 鹅
v. 戳一下（屁股）

e.en: A wild {goose} landed on the lake at sunset.
e.zh: 日落时一只野鹅落在了湖面上。

e.en: Don't {goose} the engine before it warms up.
e.zh: 发动机预热前别猛踩油门。

e.en: Grandma made a tart pie filled with fresh {gooseberry}.
e.zh: 奶奶用新鲜醋栗做了一个酸味馅饼。

e.en: The {gooseberry} bushes were heavy with green fruit in June.
e.zh: 六月里醋栗丛上挂满了青绿色的果实。

e.en: The chilly wind gave me {gooseflesh} on my arms.
e.zh: 冷风吹得我胳膊上起了一层鸡皮疙瘩。

e.en: That haunting song always raises {gooseflesh} on my neck.
e.zh: 那首萦绕心头的歌总让我脖子上起鸡皮疙瘩。

gooseneck.t: n. 鹅颈管、可弯曲支架

e.en: I clipped a {gooseneck} lamp onto the corner of my desk.
e.zh: 我把一盏鹅颈灯夹在书桌的角上。

e.en: The trailer attaches via a {gooseneck} hitch in the truck bed.
e.zh: 那辆拖车通过卡车货厢里的鹅颈式挂钩连接。

gop.t: n. 美国共和党（Grand Old Party）

e.en: The {GOP} held its primary debates earlier this month.
e.zh: 共和党本月早些时候举行了初选辩论。

e.en: Several {GOP} senators voted against the proposed bill.
e.zh: 几位共和党参议员投票反对了那项提案。

gopher.t:
n. 囊地鼠
n. Gopher 协议/Go 语言吉祥物

e.en: A {gopher} dug a network of tunnels under the lawn.
e.zh: 一只地鼠在草坪下挖了一片地道网络。

e.en: The intern was basically a {gopher} fetching coffee all day.
e.zh: 那位实习生基本就是个跑腿的,整天端咖啡。

gorbachev.t: n. 戈尔巴乔夫（苏联领导人）

e.en: {Gorbachev} introduced reforms that reshaped the Soviet Union.
e.zh: 戈尔巴乔夫推行的改革重塑了苏联。

e.en: History textbooks devote whole chapters to {Gorbachev} and glasnost.
e.zh: 历史教科书用整章篇幅讲述戈尔巴乔夫和公开化。

gorby.t: n. 戈尔巴乔夫的昵称

e.en: Western media affectionately nicknamed the Soviet leader {Gorby}.
e.zh: 西方媒体亲切地把那位苏联领导人昵称为“戈尔比”。

e.en: Cold War cartoons often depicted {Gorby} alongside Reagan.
e.zh: 冷战时期的漫画常把戈尔比和里根画在一起。

gordian.t: adj. 难解的（Gordian knot 戈尔迪之结）

e.en: The startup faced a {Gordian} tangle of legal disputes.
e.zh: 那家初创公司陷入了一团难解的法律纠纷。

e.en: She cut through the {Gordian} problem with one bold decision.
e.zh: 她用一个大胆的决定一举解开了这个棘手难题。

gore.t:
n. 凝血、血污
v. (用角) 抵伤

e.en: The horror film had way too much blood and {gore}.
e.zh: 那部恐怖片血腥场面实在太多了。

e.en: Be careful—an angry bull might {gore} you with its horns.
e.zh: 小心点——发怒的公牛可能会用角顶你。

gored.t: v. gore 的过去式；被角顶伤

e.en: The matador was {gored} by the bull during the fight.
e.zh: 那位斗牛士在比赛中被公牛顶伤。

e.en: A hiker was {gored} by a moose near the trail.
e.zh: 一名徒步者在小径附近被驼鹿顶伤。

gorge.t:
n. 峡谷
v. 狼吞虎咽

e.en: We hiked along a deep river {gorge} all afternoon.
e.zh: 我们沿着一条深深的河谷徒步走了整个下午。

e.en: Don't {gorge} yourself before the main course arrives.
e.zh: 主菜上来之前别把自己撑坏了。

e.en: The sunset over the mountains was absolutely {gorgeous}.
e.zh: 山上的日落简直美极了。

e.en: She wore a {gorgeous} red dress to the wedding.
e.zh: 她穿了一条惊艳的红色连衣裙去参加婚礼。

e.en: The garden was {gorgeously} lit for the evening reception.
e.zh: 花园为晚间招待会布置得灯光绚丽夺目。

e.en: The ballroom was {gorgeously} decorated with fresh flowers.
e.zh: 宴会厅用鲜花装饰得美轮美奂。

e.en: The sheer {gorgeousness} of the cathedral left tourists speechless.
e.zh: 大教堂那种纯粹的华美让游客们说不出话来。

e.en: Her dress was a vision of pure {gorgeousness} on stage.
e.zh: 她的礼服在舞台上展现出纯粹的惊艳之美。

gorges.t:
n. gorge 的复数
v. 狼吞虎咽

e.en: The Three {Gorges} along the Yangtze are a famous landmark.
e.zh: 长江上的三峡是一处著名的景观。

e.en: He {gorges} on chocolate every time he feels stressed.
e.zh: 他一感到压力就猛吃巧克力。

e.en: The knight's armor included a polished steel {gorget}.
e.zh: 那位骑士的盔甲里有一副擦得锃亮的钢制护喉。

e.en: The hummingbird's iridescent {gorget} flashed in the sunlight.
e.zh: 那只蜂鸟喉部的虹彩羽毛在阳光下闪闪发亮。

gorgon.t: n. 戈耳工（希腊神话蛇发女妖）

e.en: In Greek myth, a {Gorgon} could turn onlookers to stone.
e.zh: 在希腊神话中,蛇发女妖能把看到她的人变成石头。

e.en: Medusa is the most famous {Gorgon} in classical mythology.
e.zh: 美杜莎是古典神话中最有名的蛇发女妖。

gorgonzola.t: n. 戈贡佐拉蓝纹奶酪

e.en: I added crumbled {gorgonzola} to the pear and walnut salad.
e.zh: 我在梨子核桃沙拉里加了些碎戈贡佐拉奶酪。

e.en: This pasta sauce uses creamy {gorgonzola} and a splash of cream.
e.zh: 这款意面酱用了奶香浓郁的戈贡佐拉奶酪和一点鲜奶油。

gorilla.t:
n. 大猩猩
n. 彪形大汉

e.en: A massive silverback {gorilla} watched us from the trees.
e.zh: 一只巨大的银背大猩猩在树丛中注视着我们。

e.en: The zoo's new {gorilla} exhibit opens to the public tomorrow.
e.zh: 动物园新的大猩猩展区明天对公众开放。

e.en: Mountain {gorillas} live in small groups in central Africa.
e.zh: 山地大猩猩以小群体形式生活在中非地区。

e.en: Conservationists are working to protect endangered {gorillas} from poachers.
e.zh: 环保人士正努力保护濒危的大猩猩免遭偷猎。

goring.t: v. gore 的现在分词；用角顶伤

e.en: The bull's {goring} of the matador shocked the crowd.
e.zh: 公牛顶伤斗牛士的一幕震惊了观众。

e.en: He survived a near-fatal {goring} during the festival run.
e.zh: 他在节日奔牛活动中险些被牛角顶死,但幸存下来。

e.en: Maxim {Gorky} wrote powerful novels about working-class Russia.
e.zh: 马克西姆·高尔基写过许多关于俄国工人阶级的有力小说。

e.en: We strolled through {Gorky} Park on a cold Moscow afternoon.
e.zh: 在莫斯科一个寒冷的下午,我们漫步走过高尔基公园。

e.en: Tourists often {gormandize} on pasta during their first night in Rome.
e.zh: 游客在罗马的第一晚常常会大吃特吃意面。

e.en: He tends to {gormandize} whenever the buffet is unlimited.
e.zh: 只要是无限量自助餐,他就会大吃大喝。

gormless.t: adj. 笨头笨脑的、迟钝的

e.en: He gave me a {gormless} stare when I asked the question.
e.zh: 我问那个问题时,他一脸茫然地盯着我。

e.en: The sitcom features a lovable but {gormless} office intern.
e.zh: 那部情景剧里有一个讨人喜欢却呆头呆脑的办公室实习生。

gorp.t: n. 徒步干粮（坚果葡萄干混合）

e.en: I packed a bag of {gorp} for the long hike.
e.zh: 我打包了一袋什锦坚果干果,用来长途徒步。

e.en: Homemade {gorp} usually contains nuts, raisins, and chocolate chips.
e.zh: 自制的什锦干果通常包含坚果、葡萄干和巧克力豆。

e.en: Yellow {gorse} bushes covered the windswept hillsides.
e.zh: 风吹过的山坡上长满了黄色的金雀花丛。

e.en: The prickly {gorse} bloomed brightly along the coastal path.
e.zh: 沿海小径旁多刺的金雀花开得灿烂夺目。

e.en: The movie's {gory} battle scenes weren't suitable for kids.
e.zh: 那部电影血腥的战斗场面不适合小孩观看。

e.en: She spared us the {gory} details of her surgery.
e.zh: 她没把手术的血腥细节讲给我们听。

e.en: Oh {gosh}, I completely forgot about the meeting!
e.zh: 天哪,我把那个会议忘得一干二净!

e.en: {Gosh}, this coffee is way stronger than I expected.
e.zh: 哎呀,这咖啡比我想的浓多了。

e.en: A swift {goshawk} swooped down and caught the sparrow.
e.zh: 一只敏捷的苍鹰俯冲而下,抓住了那只麻雀。

e.en: Birdwatchers spotted a rare {goshawk} nesting in the pines.
e.zh: 观鸟者在松林里发现了一只稀有苍鹰筑巢。

e.en: A fuzzy yellow {gosling} waddled behind its mother.
e.zh: 一只毛茸茸的黄色小鹅摇摇摆摆地跟在妈妈后面。

e.en: The farmer hand-raised the orphaned {gosling} on his porch.
e.zh: 农夫在门廊上亲手喂养了那只成为孤儿的小鹅。

gospel.t:
n. 福音；真理
adj. 福音的

e.en: Don't take everything online as {gospel} truth.
e.zh: 别把网上看到的一切都当成绝对真理。

e.en: The choir sang a powerful {gospel} song on Sunday.
e.zh: 周日合唱团唱了一首震撼人心的福音歌曲。

gosport.t: n. 戈斯波特（英国地名）

e.en: The ferry from Portsmouth to {Gosport} runs every fifteen minutes.
e.zh: 从朴茨茅斯到戈斯波特的渡轮每十五分钟一班。

e.en: {Gosport} has a long history as a British naval town.
e.zh: 戈斯波特作为英国海军城镇有着悠久的历史。

gossamer.t:
n. 蛛丝；轻纱
adj. 轻薄的

e.en: The dress was made of {gossamer} silk that shimmered.
e.zh: 那条裙子由薄如蝉翼的丝绸制成,闪闪发亮。

e.en: Spider webs hung like {gossamer} threads in the morning light.
e.zh: 蛛网在晨光中如轻纱般悬挂着。

gossip.t:
n. 八卦；闲话
v. 说闲话

e.en: Don't believe every {gossip} you hear at the office.
e.zh: 别相信办公室里听到的每一条流言。

e.en: They love to {gossip} about their neighbors over coffee.
e.zh: 他们喜欢一边喝咖啡一边八卦邻居的事。

gossiping.t: v. 闲聊；说八卦（现在分词）

e.en: Stop {gossiping} about your coworkers behind their backs.
e.zh: 别再背地里说同事的闲话了。

e.en: The two friends spent hours {gossiping} on the phone.
e.zh: 两位朋友在电话里聊了好几个小时八卦。

gossipped.t: v. gossip 的过去式（非标准拼写）

e.en: They {gossipped} about the new manager all afternoon.
e.zh: 他们整个下午都在八卦那位新经理。

e.en: She {gossipped} with her sister about the wedding.
e.zh: 她跟姐姐聊起了那场婚礼的八卦。

gossipping.t: v. gossip 的现在分词（非标准拼写）

e.en: The teenagers were {gossipping} loudly in the cafeteria.
e.zh: 那群青少年在食堂里大声八卦着。

e.en: Stop {gossipping} and finish your homework already.
e.zh: 别再说闲话了,赶紧把作业做完。

gossips.t:
n. 八卦（复数）
v. 说闲话（第三人称）

e.en: The town {gossips} spread the news within an hour.
e.zh: 镇上那些长舌妇一小时内就把消息传开了。

e.en: She always {gossips} about celebrities with her friends.
e.zh: 她总是和朋友们八卦明星的事。

gossipy.t: adj. 爱传闲话的；充满八卦的

e.en: The magazine has a {gossipy} tone that readers love.
e.zh: 这本杂志带着读者喜爱的八卦腔调。

e.en: He's too {gossipy} to be trusted with secrets.
e.zh: 他太爱嚼舌根,不能托付秘密给他。

got.t: v. get 的过去式；拥有；明白

e.en: I {got} your message but couldn't reply right away.
e.zh: 我收到你的消息了,只是当时没法立刻回复。

e.en: She {got} promoted to senior engineer last month.
e.zh: 她上个月升为高级工程师了。

e.en: {Gotcha}, I'll send the file over right now.
e.zh: 明白了,我现在就把文件发过去。

e.en: The interview was full of {gotcha} questions.
e.zh: 那次面试满是刁难人的陷阱问题。

e.en: She dresses in {goth} style with black lace and boots.
e.zh: 她穿着哥特风格,黑色蕾丝配长靴。

e.en: The band's sound mixes {goth} with electronic music.
e.zh: 这支乐队把哥特风与电子乐混合在一起。

e.en: The {Gotha} bombers were used during the First World War.
e.zh: 哥达式轰炸机曾在第一次世界大战中使用。

e.en: He visited {Gotha} during his trip through Germany.
e.zh: 他在游览德国时去了哥达市。

gotham.t: n. 哥谭市（蝙蝠侠虚构城市）

e.en: Batman protects {Gotham} from criminals every night.
e.zh: 蝙蝠侠每晚都在保护哥谭市免受罪犯侵扰。

e.en: New Yorkers sometimes call their city {Gotham}.
e.zh: 纽约人有时把自己的城市叫作哥谭。

e.en: {Gothenburg} is the second largest city in Sweden.
e.zh: 哥德堡是瑞典第二大城市。

e.en: We took a ferry from {Gothenburg} to Denmark.
e.zh: 我们从哥德堡乘渡轮去了丹麦。

gothic.t:
adj. 哥特式的
n. 哥特风格；哥特字体

e.en: The cathedral is a stunning example of {gothic} architecture.
e.zh: 那座大教堂是哥特式建筑的惊艳代表。

e.en: She loves reading {gothic} novels with haunted castles.
e.zh: 她喜欢读那些有幽灵城堡的哥特小说。

e.en: The artist painted the landscape using vivid {gouache} colors.
e.zh: 画家用鲜艳的水粉颜料画了那幅风景。

e.en: {Gouache} dries to a matte finish unlike watercolor.
e.zh: 水粉画干后呈哑光效果,与水彩不同。

gouge.t:
v. 凿出；挖出
n. 圆凿

e.en: Be careful not to {gouge} the wooden floor with furniture.
e.zh: 小心别用家具把木地板划出凹痕。

e.en: Online scalpers {gouge} fans with outrageous ticket prices.
e.zh: 网上的黄牛用离谱的票价宰粉丝。

gouged.t: v. gouge 的过去式；挖出；敲诈

e.en: The falling rock {gouged} a deep mark into the car.
e.zh: 落下的石头在车上凿出了一道深印。

e.en: Tourists were {gouged} by overpriced taxi drivers near the airport.
e.zh: 游客在机场附近被出租车司机高价宰客。

gouging.t: v. 挖出；敲诈（现在分词）

e.en: The state is investigating price {gouging} during the storm.
e.zh: 州政府正在调查风暴期间的哄抬物价行为。

e.en: He spent hours {gouging} a pattern into the wood.
e.zh: 他花了几个小时在木头上凿出图案。

e.en: Hungarian {goulash} is a hearty stew with beef and paprika.
e.zh: 匈牙利炖牛肉是一道加红椒粉的丰盛炖菜。

e.en: My grandmother makes the best {goulash} in winter.
e.zh: 我奶奶冬天做的炖牛肉是最好吃的。

e.en: She carved a face into the dried {gourd} for decoration.
e.zh: 她在晒干的葫芦上刻了一张脸做装饰。

e.en: The farmer grows pumpkins and other {gourd} varieties.
e.zh: 那位农民种南瓜和其他葫芦科作物。

e.en: He's a true {gourmand} who travels the world for food.
e.zh: 他是个真正的美食爱好者,为美食环游世界。

e.en: The {gourmand} ordered three desserts after his main course.
e.zh: 那位贪吃客在主菜后点了三份甜点。

gourmet.t:
n. 美食家
adj. 美食的；精致的

e.en: The restaurant serves {gourmet} burgers with truffle aioli.
e.zh: 那家餐厅供应配松露蛋黄酱的高级汉堡。

e.en: She took a {gourmet} cooking class on weekends.
e.zh: 她周末上了一门精致美食烹饪课。

e.en: The festival attracts {gourmets} from across the country.
e.zh: 这个美食节吸引了来自全国各地的美食家。

e.en: Real {gourmets} appreciate the subtle flavors of this wine.
e.zh: 真正的美食家会欣赏这款酒的细腻风味。

e.en: His {gout} flares up whenever he eats too much red meat.
e.zh: 他每次吃太多红肉,痛风就会发作。

e.en: The doctor prescribed medication to manage his {gout}.
e.zh: 医生开了药来控制他的痛风。

e.en: {Gouts} of flame shot from the dragon's mouth.
e.zh: 一股股火焰从龙的口中喷出。

e.en: The volcano sent up {gouts} of ash and smoke.
e.zh: 火山喷出一团团灰烬和浓烟。

govan.t: n. 戈万（格拉斯哥地区）

e.en: {Govan} is a historic district in the city of Glasgow.
e.zh: 戈万是格拉斯哥市的一个历史悠久的区。

e.en: The shipyards in {Govan} once employed thousands of workers.
e.zh: 戈万的造船厂曾雇用了数千名工人。

e.en: Strict rules {govern} how user data is stored and shared.
e.zh: 严格的规则约束着用户数据的存储和共享方式。

e.en: It's hard to {govern} a country with so many divisions.
e.zh: 治理一个分裂如此严重的国家很困难。

governable.t: adj. 可管辖的；可控制的

e.en: The region is barely {governable} due to ongoing conflicts.
e.zh: 由于持续冲突,这个地区几乎无法治理。

e.en: A small team is more easily {governable} than a huge one.
e.zh: 小团队比大团队更容易管理。

e.en: Good {governance} requires transparency and accountability.
e.zh: 良好的治理需要透明度和问责制。

e.en: The company improved its data {governance} policies last year.
e.zh: 该公司去年完善了数据治理政策。

e.en: Different {governances} apply to public and private companies.
e.zh: 上市公司和私营公司适用不同的治理体系。

e.en: The report compares the {governances} of several democracies.
e.zh: 该报告比较了几个民主国家的治理模式。

governed.t: v. govern 的过去式；受管辖的

e.en: The colony was {governed} by appointed officials from abroad.
e.zh: 该殖民地由海外任命的官员统治。

e.en: Network access is {governed} by strict security rules.
e.zh: 网络访问由严格的安全规则管控。

e.en: The wealthy family hired a {governess} to teach their children.
e.zh: 那个富裕家庭聘请了一位家庭女教师教孩子。

e.en: Jane Eyre worked as a {governess} at Thornfield Hall.
e.zh: 简·爱在桑菲尔德庄园做家庭女教师。

governing.t:
adj. 执政的；主导的
v. 治理（现在分词）

e.en: The {governing} body announced new rules for the league.
e.zh: 管理机构宣布了联赛的新规则。

e.en: The party has been {governing} the country for a decade.
e.zh: 该党执政这个国家已经十年了。

e.en: The {government} announced new tax policies this morning.
e.zh: 政府今早宣布了新的税收政策。

e.en: Many citizens distrust the current {government}.
e.zh: 许多公民不信任现任政府。

e.en: The agency oversees several {governmental} programs nationwide.
e.zh: 该机构监管全国多项政府项目。

e.en: He works for a non-{governmental} organization in Africa.
e.zh: 他在非洲的一个非政府组织工作。

governmentally.t: adv. 由政府地；在政府方面

e.en: The project is {governmentally} funded through federal grants.
e.zh: 该项目通过联邦拨款由政府资助。

e.en: These standards are {governmentally} mandated for all manufacturers.
e.zh: 这些标准是政府对所有制造商的强制要求。

e.en: Many {governments} are racing to regulate artificial intelligence.
e.zh: 许多政府正在抢先对人工智能进行监管。

e.en: Local {governments} handle services like trash collection.
e.zh: 地方政府负责诸如垃圾回收等服务。

e.en: The {governor} signed the bill into law yesterday.
e.zh: 州长昨天签署了这项法案,使其成为法律。

e.en: She announced her campaign to run for {governor}.
e.zh: 她宣布了竞选州长的活动。

e.en: The {governorate} is divided into several smaller districts.
e.zh: 该省被划分为几个较小的区。

e.en: Cairo {governorate} is the most populous in Egypt.
e.zh: 开罗省是埃及人口最多的省。

e.en: All fifty {governors} attended the national conference.
e.zh: 全部五十位州长都出席了全国会议。

e.en: The board of {governors} meets every quarter to review progress.
e.zh: 理事会每季度开会一次审查进展。

governorship.t: n. 州长（或总督）的职位

e.en: He won the {governorship} after a tight election.
e.zh: 他在一场势均力敌的选举后赢得了州长职位。

e.en: Her {governorship} was marked by major education reforms.
e.zh: 她的州长任期以重大的教育改革著称。

governs.t: v. 管辖；统治（第三人称单数）

e.en: The constitution {governs} how laws can be changed.
e.zh: 宪法规定了法律如何修改。

e.en: Supply and demand largely {governs} market prices.
e.zh: 市场价格在很大程度上由供求关系决定。

e.en: Niel {Gow} was a famous Scottish fiddler in the 1700s.
e.zh: 尼尔·高是18世纪著名的苏格兰小提琴手。

e.en: The street was named after Captain {Gow}, a notorious pirate.
e.zh: 那条街以臭名昭著的海盗高船长命名。

e.en: The {Gower} peninsula in Wales has stunning beaches.
e.zh: 威尔士的高尔半岛拥有令人惊叹的海滩。

e.en: David {Gower} was one of England's elegant cricketers.
e.zh: 大卫·高尔是英格兰最优雅的板球手之一。

e.en: She wore a long red {gown} to the awards ceremony.
e.zh: 她穿着一袭红色长礼服出席颁奖典礼。

e.en: The patient changed into a hospital {gown} before surgery.
e.zh: 病人在手术前换上了医院的病号服。

e.en: The graduates, all {gowned} in black, walked across the stage.
e.zh: 毕业生们身穿黑色礼袍走过舞台。

e.en: Surgeons {gowned} and gloved before entering the operating room.
e.zh: 外科医生穿好手术服戴好手套后进入手术室。

e.en: The boutique sells designer {gowns} for special occasions.
e.zh: 这家精品店出售用于特殊场合的设计师礼服。

e.en: Hospital {gowns} are designed for easy access during exams.
e.zh: 医院的病号服设计便于检查时穿脱。

e.en: The {Gowrie} conspiracy remains a mystery in Scottish history.
e.zh: 高里阴谋至今仍是苏格兰历史上的一个谜。

e.en: Lake {Gowrie} is a popular weekend destination for hikers.
e.zh: 高里湖是徒步者周末常去的热门地点。

goy.t: n. 非犹太人（意第绪语）

e.en: In Yiddish, a {goy} simply refers to a non-Jewish person.
e.zh: 在意第绪语中,goy 单纯指非犹太人。

e.en: His grandmother used the word {goy} affectionately, not as an insult.
e.zh: 他奶奶用 goy 这个词带着亲昵,并非贬义。

e.en: {Goya}'s dark paintings reflect the horrors of war.
e.zh: 戈雅的黑暗画作反映了战争的恐怖。

e.en: The museum displays several etchings by Francisco {Goya}.
e.zh: 博物馆陈列着几幅弗朗西斯科·戈雅的蚀刻版画。

gpa.t: n. 平均绩点（Grade Point Average 缩写）

e.en: She graduated with a perfect 4.0 {GPA} last spring.
e.zh: 她去年春天以满分4.0的绩点毕业。

e.en: A high {GPA} alone won't guarantee admission to top universities.
e.zh: 光有高绩点并不能保证被顶尖大学录取。

gpc.t: n. 凝胶渗透色谱（缩写）

e.en: The browser sends a {GPC} signal to opt out of tracking.
e.zh: 浏览器发送GPC信号以拒绝被追踪。

e.en: Many websites still ignore the {GPC} privacy preference header.
e.zh: 许多网站仍然无视GPC隐私偏好标头。

gpo.t: n. 政府出版/印刷办公室（缩写）

e.en: The IT team pushed new security rules through {GPO} overnight.
e.zh: IT团队连夜通过组策略推送了新的安全规则。

e.en: You can disable USB ports across the domain using a {GPO}.
e.zh: 你可以用组策略对象在整个域内禁用USB端口。

gpt.t: n. 生成式预训练模型（Generative Pre-trained Transformer）

e.en: He uses {GPT} to draft emails and summarize long reports.
e.zh: 他用GPT起草邮件并总结长篇报告。

e.en: The startup fine-tuned a {GPT} model on legal documents.
e.zh: 那家初创公司在法律文件上微调了一个GPT模型。

grab.t:
v. 抓住；抢夺
n. 抓取（操作）

e.en: Let me {grab} a coffee before the meeting starts.
e.zh: 开会之前我去拿杯咖啡。

e.en: She tried to {grab} the falling vase but missed.
e.zh: 她想抓住掉落的花瓶,可惜没接住。

e.en: He {grabbed} his keys and rushed out the door.
e.zh: 他抓起钥匙就冲出了门。

e.en: The headline immediately {grabbed} my attention this morning.
e.zh: 今早那个标题一下就吸引了我的注意。

grabber.t: n. 抓取器；吸睛的东西

e.en: That opening line is a real attention {grabber}.
e.zh: 那句开场白真是个吸睛的钩子。

e.en: I used a trash {grabber} to pick up litter at the beach.
e.zh: 我用垃圾夹在海滩上捡垃圾。

grabbing.t:
v. 正在抓取
adj. 吸引人的

e.en: The toddler kept {grabbing} at the cat's tail.
e.zh: 那个小孩一直去抓猫的尾巴。

e.en: We're {grabbing} dinner downtown if you want to join.
e.zh: 我们要去市中心吃晚饭,你想一起来吗?

grabby.t: adj. 贪婪的；抓人眼球的

e.en: The kids got a bit {grabby} when the candy appeared.
e.zh: 糖果一出现,孩子们就有点抢来抢去。

e.en: That salesman was way too {grabby} with my arm.
e.zh: 那个销售员拉我胳膊也太猴急了。

grabs.t: v. 抓住（第三人称单数）

e.en: The last ticket is up for {grabs} at noon.
e.zh: 最后一张票将在中午开放抢购。

e.en: She always {grabs} the window seat on long flights.
e.zh: 长途航班上她总是抢靠窗的座位。

grace.t:
n. 优雅；恩惠
v. 使增色

e.en: The dancer moved across the stage with effortless {grace}.
e.zh: 那位舞者轻盈优雅地穿过舞台。

e.en: The bank gave us a thirty-day {grace} period to pay.
e.zh: 银行给了我们三十天的宽限期来还款。

e.en: Her exit from politics was surprisingly {graceful}.
e.zh: 她退出政坛的方式出乎意料地得体。

e.en: Swans are {graceful} on water but clumsy on land.
e.zh: 天鹅在水上优雅,在陆地上却笨拙。

e.en: He accepted the criticism {gracefully} and promised to improve.
e.zh: 他大方地接受批评,并承诺会改进。

e.en: The old building has aged {gracefully} over a century.
e.zh: 这座老建筑历经百年依然韵味十足。

e.en: The figure skater is admired for her {gracefulness} on ice.
e.zh: 这位花样滑冰选手在冰上的优雅令人赞叹。

e.en: There is a quiet {gracefulness} in the way she speaks.
e.zh: 她说话的方式里有一种安静的优雅。

e.en: The poet contrasted the {gracefulnesses} of swans and herons.
e.zh: 诗人对比了天鹅和苍鹭各自不同的优雅。

e.en: Different cultures express their own {gracefulnesses} through dance.
e.zh: 不同文化通过舞蹈展现出各自独特的优雅。

e.en: His {graceless} apology only made everyone angrier.
e.zh: 他那毫无诚意的道歉只让大家更生气。

e.en: The robot's movements looked stiff and {graceless}.
e.zh: 那个机器人的动作显得僵硬又笨拙。

e.en: He stumbled {gracelessly} across the dance floor.
e.zh: 他笨拙地跌跌撞撞地走过舞池。

e.en: The CEO exited {gracelessly} after the scandal broke.
e.zh: 丑闻曝光后,这位CEO狼狈不堪地离了职。

graces.t:
n. 风度；礼仪
v. 使生辉

e.en: She fell from his good {graces} after the argument.
e.zh: 那次争吵之后她就失去了他的青睐。

e.en: The host {graces} every dinner with witty stories.
e.zh: 主人每次晚宴都以妙趣横生的故事增色。

gracilis.t: n. 股薄肌（大腿内侧肌肉）

e.en: The {gracilis} muscle runs along the inner thigh.
e.zh: 股薄肌沿着大腿内侧延伸。

e.en: Surgeons sometimes use the {gracilis} for reconstructive grafts.
e.zh: 外科医生有时会用股薄肌做重建移植。

e.en: She was {gracious} in defeat and congratulated the winner.
e.zh: 她输得很大度,还祝贺了获胜者。

e.en: Thank you for the {gracious} welcome to your home.
e.zh: 谢谢你们如此热情地欢迎我到家里来。

e.en: The host {graciously} accepted our late arrival without complaint.
e.zh: 主人大度地接受了我们的迟到,毫无怨言。

e.en: She {graciously} declined the award and praised her teammates.
e.zh: 她婉言谢绝了奖项,并把功劳归于队友。

e.en: Her {graciousness} toward strangers won her many friends.
e.zh: 她对陌生人的友善亲切让她交到许多朋友。

e.en: The hotel is famous for the {graciousness} of its staff.
e.zh: 那家酒店以员工的彬彬有礼而闻名。

grackle.t: n. 拟八哥（一种黑色鸣禽）

e.en: A noisy {grackle} kept stealing food from our picnic.
e.zh: 一只吵闹的拟八哥不停从我们的野餐里偷食物。

e.en: The {grackle} has glossy black feathers and bright yellow eyes.
e.zh: 拟八哥有着乌黑发亮的羽毛和明亮的黄眼睛。

e.en: My sister is a recent {grad} looking for her first job.
e.zh: 我妹妹刚毕业,正在找她的第一份工作。

e.en: He's starting {grad} school in the fall to study economics.
e.zh: 他秋天就要去读研究生,主修经济学。

e.en: The painter showed a subtle {gradation} from blue to violet.
e.zh: 画家展现出从蓝色到紫色的微妙渐变。

e.en: There's a clear {gradation} of difficulty across the levels.
e.zh: 各个关卡之间难度有明显的递进。

grade.t:
n. 等级；年级；分数
v. 评分

e.en: She got a top {grade} on her chemistry exam.
e.zh: 她化学考试拿了最高分。

e.en: Teachers will {grade} the essays over the weekend.
e.zh: 老师们将在周末批改这些论文。

graded.t:
adj. 分级的
v. 评分（过去式）

e.en: The professor {graded} fifty papers in a single evening.
e.zh: 教授一个晚上就批改了五十份论文。

e.en: This trail is rated for {graded} intermediate hikers.
e.zh: 这条步道被定为中级徒步者的难度。

grader.t: n. 评分者；某年级学生

e.en: My nephew is a fifth {grader} who loves science.
e.zh: 我侄子读五年级,特别喜欢科学。

e.en: The {grader} smoothed the dirt road before paving began.
e.zh: 在铺路之前,平地机先把土路推平了。

grades.t:
n. 等级；成绩
v. 评分

e.en: Her {grades} improved dramatically after she changed schools.
e.zh: 她转学后成绩有了显著提升。

e.en: The teacher {grades} homework every Friday afternoon.
e.zh: 老师每周五下午批改作业。

e.en: The website background uses a soft pink {gradient}.
e.zh: 网站背景使用了柔和的粉色渐变。

e.en: Cyclists struggle on a steep {gradient} like that hill.
e.zh: 骑行者在那种陡坡上骑得很吃力。

grading.t:
n. 评分；分级
v. grade 的现在分词

e.en: The teacher spent all weekend {grading} final exams.
e.zh: 老师整个周末都在批改期末考试。

e.en: Diamond {grading} considers cut, color, clarity, and carat.
e.zh: 钻石分级要考虑切工、颜色、净度和克拉。

e.en: There has been a {gradual} shift toward remote work.
e.zh: 远程办公正在逐步成为趋势。

e.en: Recovery from the injury was slow and {gradual}.
e.zh: 伤势的恢复缓慢而渐进。

e.en: The party favors {gradualism} over sudden, sweeping reforms.
e.zh: 该党更倾向于渐进主义,而非剧烈的改革。

e.en: Critics argue {gradualism} delays urgent climate action.
e.zh: 批评者认为渐进主义拖慢了紧迫的气候行动。

gradualist.t:
n. 渐进主义者
adj. 渐进主义的

e.en: She takes a {gradualist} approach to organizational change.
e.zh: 她对组织变革采取循序渐进的方式。

e.en: The senator is a known {gradualist} on tax reform.
e.zh: 这位参议员在税改问题上以渐进派著称。

e.en: The pain {gradually} faded after a few days of rest.
e.zh: 休息几天后疼痛慢慢消退了。

e.en: She {gradually} learned to enjoy public speaking.
e.zh: 她渐渐开始享受公开演讲了。

graduate.t:
n. 毕业生
v. 毕业

e.en: He plans to {graduate} from college next June.
e.zh: 他打算明年六月从大学毕业。

e.en: She's pursuing a {graduate} degree in computer science.
e.zh: 她正在攻读计算机科学的研究生学位。

graduated.t:
v. 已毕业（过去式）
adj. 分级的；带刻度的

e.en: My brother {graduated} from medical school last month.
e.zh: 我哥哥上个月从医学院毕业了。

e.en: The country uses a {graduated} income tax system.
e.zh: 该国实行累进所得税制。

graduates.t:
n. 毕业生（复数）
v. 毕业（第三人称单数）

e.en: This year's {graduates} face a tough job market.
e.zh: 今年的毕业生面临严峻的就业市场。

e.en: She {graduates} from law school this coming spring.
e.zh: 她将于今年春天从法学院毕业。

graduating.t:
v. graduate 的现在分词
adj. 毕业的（如 graduating class）

e.en: He's {graduating} with honors in mechanical engineering.
e.zh: 他将以优异成绩毕业于机械工程专业。

e.en: The {graduating} class threw their caps into the air.
e.zh: 毕业班的学生把学士帽抛向了空中。

e.en: My parents flew in for my college {graduation} ceremony.
e.zh: 我父母专程飞来参加我的大学毕业典礼。

e.en: After {graduation} she moved abroad to teach English.
e.zh: 毕业后她搬到国外教英语。

graduations.t: n. 毕业典礼（复数）；刻度

e.en: Spring is full of weddings and {graduations} every year.
e.zh: 每年春天都有大量婚礼和毕业典礼。

e.en: The thermometer has tiny {graduations} marking each degree.
e.zh: 这支温度计上有标记每一度的细小刻度。

graf.t: n. 德语中的伯爵；常作姓氏

e.en: Steffi {Graf} dominated women's tennis in the early nineties.
e.zh: 史蒂菲·格拉芙在九十年代初的女子网坛独占鳌头。

e.en: The street artist signed every {graf} with the same tag.
e.zh: 那位街头艺术家在每幅涂鸦上签下同样的标记。

e.en: Colorful {graffiti} covered the walls of the abandoned warehouse.
e.zh: 五彩斑斓的涂鸦布满了废弃仓库的墙壁。

e.en: The city spent millions cleaning up illegal {graffiti} downtown.
e.zh: 该市花了数百万美元清理市中心的非法涂鸦。

graffito.t: n. 涂鸦（graffiti 的单数形式）

e.en: Archaeologists found an ancient Roman {graffito} on the wall.
e.zh: 考古学家在墙上发现了一处古罗马涂鸦。

e.en: A single {graffito} survived among the ruined frescoes.
e.zh: 在残破的壁画中只有一处涂鸦保留了下来。

graft.t:
n./v. 嫁接；移植
n. 贪污；舞弊

e.en: The surgeon performed a skin {graft} on the burn victim.
e.zh: 外科医生为烧伤者做了皮肤移植手术。

e.en: Investigators uncovered widespread {graft} in the city government.
e.zh: 调查人员揭露了市政府内普遍存在的贪腐。

grafted.t: v. graft 的过去式；已嫁接/已移植

e.en: The gardener {grafted} apple branches onto a stronger rootstock.
e.zh: 园丁把苹果枝嫁接到了更强健的砧木上。

e.en: Modern features were awkwardly {grafted} onto the old building.
e.zh: 现代化的元素被生硬地拼接到了这栋旧楼上。

grafting.t:
n. 嫁接；移植
v. graft 的现在分词

e.en: {Grafting} fruit trees takes patience and a steady hand.
e.zh: 嫁接果树需要耐心和稳定的手法。

e.en: She's {grafting} new ideas onto the company's old strategy.
e.zh: 她正把新想法嫁接到公司原有的战略上。

grafton.t: n. 格拉夫顿（地名/姓氏）

e.en: We spent the weekend hiking near {Grafton}, Vermont.
e.zh: 我们在佛蒙特州的格拉夫顿附近徒步度过了周末。

e.en: Sue {Grafton} wrote the famous alphabet mystery series.
e.zh: 苏·格拉夫顿写了著名的字母推理系列小说。

grafts.t: n. 嫁接体；移植物（复数）

e.en: Bone {grafts} can help repair severe fractures.
e.zh: 骨移植可以帮助修复严重的骨折。

e.en: He {grafts} rose stems onto stronger wild rootstocks.
e.zh: 他把玫瑰枝嫁接到更强健的野生砧木上。

e.en: She crushed some {graham} crackers for the cheesecake crust.
e.zh: 她把全麦饼干压碎,用来做芝士蛋糕的饼底。

e.en: {Graham} flour gives the bread a nutty, wholesome flavor.
e.zh: 全麦粗面粉让面包带有坚果般的天然香味。

grail.t: n. 圣杯；梦寐以求之物

e.en: A reliable cure for cancer remains the {grail} of modern medicine.
e.zh: 可靠的癌症疗法仍是现代医学的圣杯。

e.en: Knights once searched far and wide for the holy {grail}.
e.zh: 骑士们曾四处寻找圣杯。

e.en: Farmers store {grain} in tall silos near the railway.
e.zh: 农民把谷物储存在铁路旁的高大筒仓里。

e.en: You can clearly see the {grain} of the oak tabletop.
e.zh: 你能清楚地看到橡木桌面的纹理。

grained.t: adj. 有纹理的；有颗粒的

e.en: The carpenter chose a fine-{grained} walnut for the cabinet.
e.zh: 木匠选了纹理细腻的胡桃木来做柜子。

e.en: She prefers coarse-{grained} salt for finishing dishes.
e.zh: 她喜欢用颗粒粗的盐为菜肴调味。

e.en: The photo's {graininess} gives it a vintage, film-like feel.
e.zh: 照片的颗粒感赋予它复古的胶片质感。

e.en: Cooks dislike the {graininess} of overcooked custard.
e.zh: 厨师不喜欢过火蛋奶酱产生的颗粒感。

e.en: Whole {grains} are an important part of a healthy diet.
e.zh: 全谷物是健康饮食的重要组成部分。

e.en: A few {grains} of sand were stuck in her shoe.
e.zh: 她鞋里卡了几粒沙子。

grainy.t: adj. 有颗粒感的（常形容图像、照片）

e.en: The old security footage looks dark and {grainy}.
e.zh: 那段旧监控录像看起来又暗又有颗粒感。

e.en: The peanut butter has a slightly {grainy} texture.
e.zh: 这款花生酱口感略带颗粒。

e.en: Add ten {gram} of sugar to the cookie batter.
e.zh: 在饼干面糊里加入十克糖。

e.en: The pharmacist weighed exactly one {gram} of powder.
e.zh: 药剂师精确称量了一克粉末。

grama.t: n. 格兰马草（北美草原牧草）

e.en: Cattle graze on {grama} grass across the open prairie.
e.zh: 牛群在开阔的草原上啃食格兰马草。

e.en: Drought-tolerant {grama} thrives in the dry Southwest.
e.zh: 耐旱的格兰马草在干燥的西南地区长势良好。

e.en: My {gramma} bakes the best apple pie every Sunday.
e.zh: 我奶奶每周日都做最好吃的苹果派。

e.en: The kids ran to hug their {gramma} at the door.
e.zh: 孩子们跑到门口拥抱奶奶。

e.en: English {grammar} can be tricky for beginners to master.
e.zh: 英语语法对初学者来说可能很难掌握。

e.en: The app highlights {grammar} mistakes as you type.
e.zh: 这款应用会在你输入时标出语法错误。

e.en: A strict {grammarian} would never accept that sentence.
e.zh: 严格的语法学家绝不会接受那个句子。

e.en: The famous {grammarian} wrote a definitive guide to English usage.
e.zh: 那位著名的语法学家写了一本权威的英语用法指南。

grammatical.t: adj. 语法的；符合语法的

e.en: Please correct any {grammatical} errors before submitting the essay.
e.zh: 提交论文前请改正所有语法错误。

e.en: The sentence is {grammatical} but sounds a bit awkward.
e.zh: 这句话语法正确,但听起来有点别扭。

grammatically.t: adv. 语法上；在语法方面

e.en: The translation is {grammatically} correct yet feels unnatural.
e.zh: 译文语法正确,但读起来不自然。

e.en: Children gradually learn to speak {grammatically} as they grow.
e.zh: 孩子们随着成长逐渐学会按语法说话。

gramme.t: n. 克（gram 的英式拼写）

e.en: The recipe calls for one {gramme} of saffron threads.
e.zh: 这道食谱需要一克藏红花丝。

e.en: Each tablet contains half a {gramme} of the active ingredient.
e.zh: 每片药含半克活性成分。

e.en: Add two hundred {grammes} of flour to the mixture.
e.zh: 在混合物中加入两百克面粉。

e.en: The package weighs about fifty {grammes}.
e.zh: 这个包裹大约重五十克。

e.en: The singer won her first {grammy} at age nineteen.
e.zh: 这位歌手十九岁就赢得了她的第一座格莱美奖。

e.en: Critics predict the album will earn a {grammy} nomination.
e.zh: 评论家预测这张专辑会获得格莱美提名。

e.en: He collects old jazz records to play on his {gramophone}.
e.zh: 他收集老爵士唱片,在他的留声机上播放。

e.en: The antique {gramophone} still produces a warm, crackling sound.
e.zh: 这台古董留声机仍能发出温暖的沙沙声。

e.en: {Grampa} taught me how to whistle when I was six.
e.zh: 我六岁时,爷爷教我吹口哨。

e.en: Every summer, we visit {grampa} at his cabin.
e.zh: 每年夏天,我们都去爷爷的小木屋看他。

grampian.t: n. 格兰扁（苏格兰地区名）

e.en: We hiked through the {grampian} mountains last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末我们在格兰扁山脉徒步旅行。

e.en: The {grampian} region is known for its whisky distilleries.
e.zh: 格兰扁地区以其威士忌酒厂而闻名。

gramps.t: n. 爷爷（口语，亲昵称呼）

e.en: Hey {gramps}, can you help me fix this bike?
e.zh: 嘿爷爷,你能帮我修这辆自行车吗?

e.en: {Gramps} always tells the funniest stories at dinner.
e.zh: 爷爷总在晚饭时讲最有趣的故事。

e.en: The recipe needs three hundred {grams} of dark chocolate.
e.zh: 这道食谱需要三百克黑巧克力。

e.en: Add fifty {grams} of butter and stir until smooth.
e.zh: 加入五十克黄油,搅拌至顺滑。

gramsci.t: n. 葛兰西（意大利思想家）

e.en: Many scholars still cite {gramsci} when discussing cultural hegemony.
e.zh: 许多学者在讨论文化霸权时仍会引用葛兰西。

e.en: {Gramsci} wrote his most influential works while in prison.
e.zh: 葛兰西在狱中写下了他最具影响力的著作。

gran.t: n. 奶奶；外婆（英式口语）

e.en: My {gran} knits the warmest sweaters every winter.
e.zh: 我奶奶每年冬天都织最暖和的毛衣。

e.en: We're going to {gran}'s house for tea this Sunday.
e.zh: 这周日我们要去奶奶家喝茶。

granada.t: n. 格拉纳达（西班牙城市）

e.en: The Alhambra palace in {granada} attracts millions of tourists yearly.
e.zh: 格拉纳达的阿尔罕布拉宫每年吸引数百万游客。

e.en: We spent three days exploring the old streets of {granada}.
e.zh: 我们花了三天时间探索格拉纳达的老街。

e.en: Ukraine has long been called the {granary} of Europe.
e.zh: 乌克兰长期以来被称为欧洲的粮仓。

e.en: The wooden {granary} stored enough wheat for the whole village.
e.zh: 那座木制谷仓储存的小麦够整个村庄食用。

e.en: We rented a cabin near {granby} for our ski trip.
e.zh: 我们在格兰比附近租了一间小木屋去滑雪。

e.en: The town of {granby} sits beside a beautiful mountain lake.
e.zh: 格兰比小镇坐落在一座美丽的山中湖畔。

grand.t:
adj. 宏伟的；盛大的
n. 一千美元（俚）

e.en: They held the wedding in a {grand} ballroom downtown.
e.zh: 他们在市中心一个豪华舞厅举行了婚礼。

e.en: That was a {grand} performance by the entire team.
e.zh: 整支队伍的表现真是棒极了。

e.en: My {grandad} served in the navy during the war.
e.zh: 我爷爷战时在海军服役。

e.en: {Grandad} reads the newspaper on the porch every morning.
e.zh: 爷爷每天早上都在门廊上看报纸。

e.en: The Boston Marathon is the {grandaddy} of all road races.
e.zh: 波士顿马拉松是所有公路赛跑的鼻祖。

e.en: My {grandaddy} grew up on a small Texas farm.
e.zh: 我爷爷在德州一个小农场长大。

e.en: She showed everyone photos of her newborn {grandbaby}.
e.zh: 她向大家展示她刚出生的小孙子的照片。

e.en: The {grandbaby} giggled as grandpa made silly faces.
e.zh: 爷爷做着鬼脸,小孙子咯咯地笑。

grandchild.t: n. 孙子/孙女；外孙/外孙女

e.en: Her first {grandchild} was born early Sunday morning.
e.zh: 她的第一个孙子在周日清晨出生了。

e.en: He spoils every {grandchild} with cookies and bedtime stories.
e.zh: 他用饼干和睡前故事宠爱每一个孙辈。

e.en: All five {grandchildren} came home for the holidays.
e.zh: 五个孙辈都回家过节了。

e.en: She loves reading bedtime stories to her {grandchildren}.
e.zh: 她喜欢给孙辈们读睡前故事。

e.en: My {granddad} taught me how to fish when I was young.
e.zh: 我小时候,爷爷教我钓鱼。

e.en: {Granddad} still drives himself to the grocery store.
e.zh: 爷爷还能自己开车去杂货店。

e.en: The internet is the {granddaddy} of modern communication tools.
e.zh: 互联网是现代通信工具的鼻祖。

e.en: My {granddaddy} owned the local hardware store for decades.
e.zh: 我爷爷经营当地的五金店有几十年了。

e.en: Both of my {granddads} fought in World War II.
e.zh: 我的两位爷爷都参加过第二次世界大战。

e.en: The park was full of {granddads} pushing strollers.
e.zh: 公园里满是推着婴儿车的爷爷们。

e.en: His {granddaughter} just graduated from medical school.
e.zh: 他的孙女刚刚从医学院毕业。

e.en: Grandma knitted a tiny sweater for her newborn {granddaughter}.
e.zh: 奶奶为刚出生的孙女织了一件小毛衣。

e.en: She has three {granddaughters} who all play soccer.
e.zh: 她有三个孙女,都踢足球。

e.en: The two {granddaughters} sang together at grandma's birthday.
e.zh: 两个孙女在奶奶生日时一起唱歌。

grande.t:
adj. 大号的（星巴克中杯）
n. 格兰德

e.en: I'll have a {grande} latte with oat milk, please.
e.zh: 请给我一杯燕麦奶大杯拿铁。

e.en: She always orders a {grande} iced coffee in the morning.
e.zh: 她早上总是点一杯大杯冰咖啡。

e.en: The Spanish {grandee} owned vast estates across the country.
e.zh: 那位西班牙大公在全国拥有大片庄园。

e.en: He acted like a political {grandee} at the dinner party.
e.zh: 他在晚宴上表现得像位政界大佬。

e.en: Visitors are stunned by the {grandeur} of the cathedral.
e.zh: 游客们被这座大教堂的宏伟所震撼。

e.en: The film captures the {grandeur} of the Himalayan peaks.
e.zh: 这部电影捕捉到了喜马拉雅群峰的壮丽。

grandfather.t:
n. 祖父；外公
v. 保留旧规则

e.en: My {grandfather} immigrated from Italy in the 1950s.
e.zh: 我祖父在 1950 年代从意大利移民过来。

e.en: The old {grandfather} clock chimes every hour at midnight.
e.zh: 那座老式落地钟每到整点就敲响一次。

grandfathered.t: v. 依旧规豁免（新规不适用）

e.en: Existing customers were {grandfathered} into the original pricing plan.
e.zh: 老用户被沿用在原来的定价方案中。

e.en: His license was {grandfathered} when the new rules took effect.
e.zh: 新规生效时,他的执照按旧规定继续有效。

grandfatherly.t: adj. 像祖父一样的；慈祥的

e.en: The doctor's {grandfatherly} smile put the children at ease.
e.zh: 医生那慈祥的笑容让孩子们放下了戒心。

e.en: He offered {grandfatherly} advice over a cup of tea.
e.zh: 他一边喝茶一边给出长辈般的建议。

e.en: Both of her {grandfathers} were carpenters in the same town.
e.zh: 她的两位祖父都是同一座小镇的木匠。

e.en: The {grandfathers} swapped war stories over a glass of whisky.
e.zh: 几位爷爷一边喝威士忌一边交流战时的故事。

grandiloquent.t: adj. 夸夸其谈的；浮夸的

e.en: His {grandiloquent} speech bored the audience to tears.
e.zh: 他那夸夸其谈的演讲让观众听得昏昏欲睡。

e.en: Politicians often make {grandiloquent} promises during election season.
e.zh: 政客们在竞选期间常做出夸大其辞的承诺。

grandiose.t: adj. 浮夸的；自命不凡的

e.en: The startup has {grandiose} plans but very little funding.
e.zh: 这家初创公司计划宏大,但资金却很少。

e.en: His {grandiose} mansion seemed out of place in the village.
e.zh: 他那座豪华的宅邸在村里显得格格不入。

e.en: He {grandiosely} announced a project no one believed in.
e.zh: 他夸张地宣布了一项无人相信的项目。

e.en: The CEO {grandiosely} promised to revolutionize the entire industry.
e.zh: 那位首席执行官夸夸其谈地承诺要彻底变革整个行业。

e.en: Critics mocked the film's {grandiosity} and weak storyline.
e.zh: 评论家嘲讽这部电影故作宏大,故事却很薄弱。

e.en: His {grandiosity} hides deep personal insecurities.
e.zh: 他的浮夸自大背后藏着深深的不安全感。

e.en: She brought her youngest {grandkid} to the playground today.
e.zh: 她今天带最小的孙子去了游乐场。

e.en: Every {grandkid} got a handmade sweater for Christmas.
e.zh: 每个孙辈圣诞节都收到一件手织毛衣。

e.en: He {grandly} declared that he would change the world.
e.zh: 他夸张地宣称自己要改变世界。

e.en: The hotel lobby was {grandly} decorated with marble and gold.
e.zh: 酒店大堂用大理石和金饰装饰得富丽堂皇。

e.en: My {grandma} bakes the best apple pie every Sunday.
e.zh: 我奶奶每个星期天都会烤最好吃的苹果派。

e.en: {Grandma} taught me how to knit a scarf.
e.zh: 奶奶教我怎么织围巾。

e.en: The little girl ran to hug her {grandmama}.
e.zh: 小女孩跑过去抱住了她的外婆。

e.en: {Grandmama} always keeps candy in her purse.
e.zh: 外婆的手提包里总是放着糖果。

e.en: Both {grandmas} came to watch the school play.
e.zh: 两位奶奶都来看学校的话剧表演了。

e.en: Many {grandmas} love spoiling their grandchildren.
e.zh: 很多奶奶都喜欢宠爱自己的孙辈。

grandmaster.t: n. 国际象棋特级大师；宗师

e.en: He became a chess {grandmaster} at just fourteen.
e.zh: 他十四岁就成为了国际象棋特级大师。

e.en: The {grandmaster} analyzed every move with precision.
e.zh: 那位特级大师精确地分析了每一步棋。

e.en: My {grandmother} lived through the war years.
e.zh: 我祖母经历过那些战争年代。

e.en: She inherited the ring from her {grandmother}.
e.zh: 她从祖母那里继承了那枚戒指。

grandmotherly.t: adj. 像祖母一样的；慈祥的

e.en: The nurse spoke in a warm, {grandmotherly} tone.
e.zh: 那位护士用温暖、慈祥的语气说话。

e.en: She gave him a {grandmotherly} pat on the cheek.
e.zh: 她像奶奶一样轻拍了他的脸颊。

e.en: Both my {grandmothers} are still in good health.
e.zh: 我的两位祖母身体都还很硬朗。

e.en: Many {grandmothers} help raise their grandchildren today.
e.zh: 如今许多祖母都在帮忙带孙辈。

e.en: She knitted a sweater for her newborn {grandnephew}.
e.zh: 她为刚出生的侄孙织了一件毛衣。

e.en: My {grandnephew} just started kindergarten this fall.
e.zh: 我的侄孙今年秋天刚上幼儿园。

e.en: The {grandness} of the cathedral left visitors speechless.
e.zh: 大教堂的宏伟壮丽让游客们说不出话来。

e.en: There's a certain {grandness} to the old hotel's lobby.
e.zh: 那家老酒店的大堂有一种独特的气派。

e.en: He sent his {grandniece} a birthday card every year.
e.zh: 他每年都给侄孙女寄一张生日卡。

e.en: My {grandniece} just learned to ride a bike.
e.zh: 我的侄孙女刚刚学会骑自行车。

e.en: {Grandpa} tells the funniest stories at dinner.
e.zh: 爷爷在晚饭时讲的故事最好笑了。

e.en: My {grandpa} still drives to the market every morning.
e.zh: 我爷爷每天早上还自己开车去市场。

e.en: Becoming a {grandparent} changed his whole outlook on life.
e.zh: 成为祖父辈彻底改变了他对人生的看法。

e.en: Every child should know at least one {grandparent}.
e.zh: 每个孩子都应该至少认识一位祖辈。

e.en: We visit my {grandparents} during the summer holidays.
e.zh: 我们暑假会去看望我的爷爷奶奶。

e.en: Her {grandparents} immigrated from Italy in the 1950s.
e.zh: 她的祖父母在上世纪五十年代从意大利移民过来。

e.en: Both {grandpas} showed up to cheer at the game.
e.zh: 两位爷爷都到场为比赛加油。

e.en: Some {grandpas} love telling old war stories.
e.zh: 有些爷爷特别喜欢讲过去的战争故事。

e.en: She paid two {grands} for that secondhand laptop.
e.zh: 她花了两千块买了那台二手笔记本电脑。

e.en: The vintage watch sold for twenty {grands} online.
e.zh: 那块复古手表在网上以两万元成交。

e.en: Her {grandson} just graduated from medical school.
e.zh: 她的孙子刚刚从医学院毕业。

e.en: He taught his {grandson} how to fish at the lake.
e.zh: 他在湖边教孙子怎么钓鱼。

e.en: All three {grandsons} look exactly like their father.
e.zh: 三个孙子长得都跟他们父亲一模一样。

e.en: Her {grandsons} visit every weekend without fail.
e.zh: 她的几个孙子每个周末都会来看她。

grandstand.t:
n. 大看台
v. 哗众取宠

e.en: The crowd in the {grandstand} cheered loudly for the team.
e.zh: 看台上的观众大声为球队欢呼。

e.en: Politicians often {grandstand} during televised debates.
e.zh: 政客们经常在电视辩论中哗众取宠。

e.en: His {grandstanding} during the meeting annoyed everyone.
e.zh: 他在会议中的哗众取宠让所有人都很反感。

e.en: The senator was accused of {grandstanding} for media attention.
e.zh: 那位参议员被指责为博取媒体关注而作秀。

e.en: They bought an old stone {grange} in the countryside.
e.zh: 他们在乡下买了一座古老的石砌庄园。

e.en: The {grange} hosted the annual harvest festival.
e.zh: 那座庄园举办了一年一度的丰收节。

grangemouth.t: n. 格兰杰茅斯（苏格兰地名）

e.en: The oil refinery at {Grangemouth} employs thousands of workers.
e.zh: 格兰其茅斯的炼油厂雇用了数千名工人。

e.en: {Grangemouth} is a major port town in Scotland.
e.zh: 格兰其茅斯是苏格兰的一个主要港口城镇。

e.en: The old {granger} knew every field on the farm.
e.zh: 那位老农夫熟悉农场里的每一块田地。

e.en: Her grandfather worked as a {granger} for decades.
e.zh: 她爷爷做了几十年的农场管理员。

e.en: On hot days, I love a lemon {granita} from the cafe.
e.zh: 天热的时候,我喜欢在咖啡馆来一杯柠檬冰沙。

e.en: Sicilian {granita} is traditionally served with brioche.
e.zh: 西西里冰沙传统上会配着布里欧修面包一起吃。

e.en: The kitchen counters are made of polished black {granite}.
e.zh: 厨房的台面是用抛光的黑色花岗岩做的。

e.en: Climbers love the rough {granite} cliffs of Yosemite.
e.zh: 攀岩者喜爱优胜美地粗糙的花岗岩峭壁。

e.en: The mountain has a hard, {granitic} core beneath the soil.
e.zh: 那座山的土壤下面有坚硬的花岗岩岩芯。

e.en: Geologists studied the {granitic} rocks of the region.
e.zh: 地质学家研究了该地区的花岗岩岩层。

grannie.t: n. 奶奶；外婆（granny 的变体）

e.en: My {grannie} still sends me handwritten letters.
e.zh: 我奶奶还坚持给我写手写信。

e.en: {Grannie} makes the most amazing chocolate cookies.
e.zh: 奶奶做的巧克力饼干是最棒的。

grannies.t: n. 奶奶们（granny 的复数）

e.en: The two {grannies} chatted on the park bench all afternoon.
e.zh: 两位老奶奶在公园长椅上聊了一下午。

e.en: Some {grannies} are surprisingly skilled with smartphones.
e.zh: 有些老奶奶用智能手机出奇地熟练。

e.en: My {granny} taught me how to bake bread from scratch.
e.zh: 我奶奶教我从头开始烤面包。

e.en: He tied the rope into a clumsy {granny} knot.
e.zh: 他把绳子打成了一个笨拙的老奶奶结。

granola.t: n. 格兰诺拉麦片（燕麦坚果早餐）

e.en: I sprinkle {granola} on my yogurt every morning.
e.zh: 我每天早上都会在酸奶上撒些格兰诺拉麦片。

e.en: Homemade {granola} tastes much better than store-bought.
e.zh: 自制的格兰诺拉麦片比商店买的好吃多了。

grant.t:
v. 授予；准予
n. 拨款；补助金

e.en: The university received a research {grant} from the government.
e.zh: 这所大学获得了政府的一笔研究资助。

e.en: The judge agreed to {grant} the appeal.
e.zh: 法官同意准许这次上诉。

granta.t: n. 格兰塔（英国文学杂志名）

e.en: She subscribed to {Granta} for its literary fiction.
